stories.canonicalTitle: Demeter and Persephone

stories.summaryZh: 珀耳塞福涅被带往冥界后，得墨忒耳离开诸神寻找女儿；本页严格以《荷马颂歌·致得墨忒耳》的见证范围叙述。

versions.rightsNote: 须署名 Te Ahukaramū Charles Royal 与 Te Ara；只发布公开页面的独立概述，不收集具名部族版本。

sections.bodyZh: Te Ara 写道：在毛利传统中，创世的核心行动是天与地的分离。故事从黑暗与虚无开始，天父兰吉努伊与地母帕帕图阿努库从中出现。起初天地紧紧相连，他们的孩子就出生在两者之间。
sections.bodyEn: Te Ara writes that in Māori tradition the central act of creation is the separation of earth and sky. The story begins in darkness and nothingness, from which Ranginui the sky father and Papatūānuku the earth mother emerge. At first earth and sky are joined, and their children are born between them.
sections.evidenceNote: Te Ara“毛利创世传统”第1页。

sections.bodyZh: 孩子们决定把父母分开。天与地一旦分离，光就照进了世界——从黑暗走向光明，正是由孩子们的这一行动完成的。
sections.bodyEn: The children decide to separate their parents. Once earth and sky are apart, light enters the world: the move from darkness to light is achieved by the children's act.
sections.uncertaintyNote: Te Ara 说明：在部分部族版本中，塔内在分开天地时起重要作用；本站不选定某一部族的说法。

sections.bodyZh: 分离之后，孩子们成为自然各部分的神（atua）：塔内是森林之神，塔加罗阿是海洋之神，还有地震之神鲁奥莫科、风与天气之神塔维里马特阿。把这些神编进同一个谱系，是毛利人解释自然世界的传统方式。
sections.bodyEn: After the separation the children become atua of different parts of nature: Tāne of the forests, Tangaroa of the sea, Rūaumoko of earthquakes, Tāwhirimātea of winds and weather. Weaving these atua into one genealogy is the traditional Māori way of explaining the natural world.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 鲁奥莫科与塔维里马特阿尚未建立独立实体。

sections.bodyZh: Te Ara 也提醒，各部族的创世故事差异很大，特别是关于至高存在的角色。这里只讲公开页面所总结的共同线索，具名部族的版本须经相应权威授权。
sections.bodyEn: Te Ara also cautions that tribal versions vary considerably, especially on the role of a supreme being. This retelling covers only the common threads the public page summarizes; named iwi versions require permission from the appropriate authority.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 具名 iwi／hapū 版本仍为权限阻塞。

stories.canonicalTitle: Nüwa repairs the sky — Huainanzi and Liezi witnesses
stories.titleZh: 女娲补天：《淮南子》与《列子》两种见证
stories.summaryZh: 《淮南子·览冥训》与《列子·汤问》都记载女娲炼五色石、断鳌足立四极；前者另有黑龙与芦灰，后者把补天放在天地“物有不足”的问答里，并在其后才引出共工。两份见证分开阅读，不合成后世“共工撞山导致女娲补天”的版本。
stories.summaryEn: Huainanzi “Lan Ming” and Liezi “Tang Wen” both have Nüwa refine five-colored stones and cut a turtle's legs to set up the four poles; the former adds the black dragon and reed ash, while the latter frames the repair as a remedy for deficient things and introduces Gonggong only afterwards. The two witnesses are read separately and are not merged into the later version in which Gonggong's collision causes the repair.
stories.editorialNote: 两份传世文献逐段并列；《列子》传世本成书年代有争议，不据此排序。后世因果化的复述作为独立接受层排队。

conflicts.summary: Liezi Tang Wen places the Gonggong collision after Nüwa's repair, while Huainanzi Tian Wen narrates it as a standalone cosmological etiology without Nüwa.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep both placements. Do not adopt the later retelling in which the collision causes the repair until that reception layer is registered with exact locators.
conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Liezi Tang Wen witness the Gonggong episode is introduced with 其後 after Nüwa's repair.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Huainanzi Tian Wen witness narrates the Gonggong collision on its own as an explanation of cosmic orientation without naming Nüwa.
conflicts.storyNotes: The Liezi witness attaches Gonggong after the repair; no causal synthesis.

sections.bodyZh: 《淮南子·览冥训》以远古为背景：支撑天地的四极崩坏，九州开裂，天不能全覆、地不能全载，大火与洪水都无法止息，猛兽鸷鸟危害百姓。本段只按这一见证的顺序概述，不补入其他文献给出的起因。
sections.bodyEn: Huainanzi “Lan Ming” sets the scene in remote antiquity: the four poles holding up the world have failed and the nine provinces have split; heaven no longer covers everything and earth no longer bears everything, fires and floods cannot be stopped, and wild beasts and birds of prey attack the people. This section follows only this witness and adds no cause taken from other texts.
sections.evidenceNote: 《淮南子·览冥训》“往古之时”段；Chinese Text Project 章节页。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 传世本用字存在异体；本站只发布独立概述，不复制整段原文。

sections.headingEn: Five-colored stones and the turtle's legs
sections.bodyZh: 于是女娲炼五色石来修补苍天，又截断巨鳌的足，用来重新立起四极。
sections.bodyEn: Nüwa then refines five-colored stones to patch the azure sky and cuts off the legs of a great turtle to set the four poles upright again.
sections.evidenceNote: 同段女娲补天与立四极的句组。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 炼字与鳌字在不同版本中有异体，不影响本段概述。

sections.headingEn: The black dragon and the reed ash
sections.bodyZh: 这一见证还写到女娲杀死黑龙以救济冀州，并堆积芦苇灰来堵住泛滥的洪水；随后天地重新安定，百姓得以存活。
sections.bodyEn: This witness adds that Nüwa kills a black dragon to relieve Jizhou and piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters; afterwards heaven and earth are set right and the people survive.
sections.evidenceNote: 同段黑龙、冀州与芦灰句组。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 冀州在此是文本中的九州之一，不映射为现代行政区或坐标；《列子·汤问》对应段落未陈述这两项。

sections.bodyZh: 《览冥训》的女娲段落没有把天地崩坏归因于共工。《淮南子》确实在《天文训》另记共工怒触不周山，但那是另一章中独立的天地倾斜起源，本站不把两章拼接成因果链。
sections.bodyEn: The Lan Ming Nüwa passage does not attribute the collapse to Gonggong. The Huainanzi does narrate Gonggong striking Mount Buzhou, but in a separate passage in the “Tian Wen” chapter that explains the tilt of heaven and earth; the site does not splice the two chapters into a causal chain.
sections.evidenceNote: 《览冥训》女娲段与《天文训》共工段分别定位。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 把共工触山写成女娲补天起因的说法见于较晚文献，已作为独立接受层排队。

events.summaryZh: 四极崩坏、九州开裂。
events.summaryEn: The four poles fail and the nine provinces split.
events.uncertaintyNote: 宇宙性的崩坏不投射为现实地点。

events.titleEn: Patching the sky and setting the poles
events.summaryZh: 女娲用五色石与鳌足修复天地。
events.summaryEn: Nüwa repairs the world with the stones and the turtle's legs.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 杀黑龙、积芦灰止水。
events.summaryEn: The black dragon is killed and reed ash stops the floods.
events.uncertaintyNote: 冀州是文本中的九州之一，不映射为现代坐标。

events.summaryZh: 本段不含共工，不与《天文训》拼接。
events.summaryEn: No Gonggong here; not spliced with “Tian Wen”.
events.uncertaintyNote: 这是来源边界节点，不是新增神话动作。

sections.headingEn: Heaven and earth are also things
sections.bodyZh: 《列子·汤问》把女娲补天放在殷汤与夏革关于天地有无极限的问答中：天地也是物，物都有不足之处，所以古时女娲修补了它的缺口。
sections.bodyEn: Liezi “Tang Wen” places the repair inside a dialogue between Tang of Yin and Xia Ge on whether heaven and earth have limits: heaven and earth are also things, things have deficiencies, and so in antiquity Nüwa mended the gap.
sections.evidenceNote: 《列子·汤问》殷汤与夏革问答段。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 《列子》托名列御寇，传世本成书年代有争议；本站不据此把它排在《淮南子》之前。

sections.headingEn: Five-colored stones and the turtle's legs
sections.bodyZh: 这一见证同样写女娲炼五色石补其缺口，并截断鳌足以立四极；它没有写黑龙、冀州或芦灰。
sections.bodyEn: This witness likewise has Nüwa refine five-colored stones to fill the gap and cut the turtle's legs to set up the four poles; it does not mention the black dragon, Jizhou or reed ash.
sections.uncertaintyNote: “未陈述”只描述本段范围，不是对《淮南子》细节的否定。

sections.bodyZh: 紧接补天之后，《汤问》用“其后”引出共工氏与颛顼争为帝、怒触不周之山。在这一见证里，共工事件发生在女娲补天之后，而不是它的起因。
sections.bodyEn: Right after the repair, “Tang Wen” uses “afterwards” to introduce Gonggong contending with Zhuanxu for rulership and striking Mount Buzhou in anger. In this witness the Gonggong episode follows Nüwa's repair; it is not its cause.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 后世“共工触山导致女娲补天”的因果顺序不回写进本见证。

sections.headingEn: Heaven tilts northwest, waters gather southeast
sections.bodyZh: 共工撞山折断天柱、断绝地维，于是天向西北倾斜，日月星辰向那里移动；地在东南不满，众水因此流归东南。
sections.bodyEn: Gonggong's blow breaks the pillar of heaven and snaps the cords of the earth, so heaven tilts toward the northwest, where the sun, moon and stars move, and the earth falls short in the southeast, where the rivers and flood waters gather.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是文本中的天地形势起源解释，不作为地理或天文史实。

events.summaryEn: Heaven and earth are treated as deficient things.
events.uncertaintyNote: 问答框架节点。

stories.canonicalTitle: Gonggong strikes Mount Buzhou — two early witnesses
stories.titleZh: 共工触不周山：天倾西北的两处见证
stories.summaryZh: 《淮南子·天文训》把共工与颛顼争帝、怒触不周山写成独立的天地倾斜起源；《列子·汤问》则用“其后”把同一事件接在女娲补天之后。两处见证都不把它写成女娲补天的起因。
stories.summaryEn: Huainanzi “Tian Wen” narrates Gonggong contending with Zhuanxu and striking Mount Buzhou as a standalone explanation of why heaven and earth tilt; Liezi “Tang Wen” attaches the same event after Nüwa's repair with “afterwards”. Neither witness makes it the cause of Nüwa's repair.
stories.editorialNote: 事件位置差异进入显式冲突档案；不周山不投射为现实坐标，颛顼不作历史真实性判断。

conflicts.summary: Liezi Tang Wen places the Gonggong collision after Nüwa's repair, while Huainanzi Tian Wen narrates it as a standalone cosmological etiology without Nüwa.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep both placements. Do not adopt the later retelling in which the collision causes the repair until that reception layer is registered with exact locators.
conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Liezi Tang Wen witness the Gonggong episode is introduced with 其後 after Nüwa's repair.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Huainanzi Tian Wen witness narrates the Gonggong collision on its own as an explanation of cosmic orientation without naming Nüwa.
conflicts.storyNotes: Standalone etiology versus sequel to Nüwa's repair.

witnessComparisons.editorialNoteEn: Both share the collision, the broken pillar and the northwest tilt; the wording differs slightly.

sections.bodyZh: 《淮南子·天文训》说，从前共工与颛顼争夺帝位。
sections.bodyEn: Huainanzi “Tian Wen” says that long ago Gonggong contended with Zhuanxu to become ruler.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 颛顼在此作为传说中的君主登记，不作历史真实性判断。

sections.bodyZh: 共工发怒撞向不周山，支撑天的柱子折断，系住大地的绳索断绝。
sections.bodyEn: In anger Gonggong strikes Mount Buzhou; the pillar holding up heaven breaks and the cords binding the earth snap.
sections.evidenceNote: 同段不周山、天柱与地维句组。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 不周山不映射为现代山名或坐标。

sections.bodyZh: 结果天向西北倾斜，日月星辰随之移动；地在东南不满，积水与尘埃都归向那里。这一段没有提到女娲，是《天文训》中独立的天地形势解释。
sections.bodyEn: As a result heaven tilts to the northwest and the sun, moon and stars shift with it; the earth falls short in the southeast, where waters and dust collect. The passage does not mention Nüwa and stands as an independent explanation of cosmic orientation in “Tian Wen”.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 同书《览冥训》的女娲段与此段分属不同章节，不合成单一故事。

events.summaryZh: 共工与颛顼争帝。
events.summaryEn: Gonggong contends with Zhuanxu.
events.uncertaintyNote: 当前见证未定位争帝地点。

events.summaryZh: 天柱折、地维绝。
events.summaryEn: The pillar of heaven breaks and the cords of earth snap.
events.uncertaintyNote: 不周山不映射为现代山名。

events.summaryZh: 天倾西北、地不满东南；不含女娲。
events.summaryEn: Heaven tilts northwest, earth falls short southeast; no Nüwa.
events.uncertaintyNote: 与《列子》的位置差异进入显式冲突档案。

sections.bodyEn: Liezi “Tang Wen” turns to Gonggong with “afterwards” right after narrating Nüwa's repair, so in this witness the Gonggong episode has an explicit place in sequence.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 叙事先后只属于这一见证，不是绝对年代。

sections.bodyZh: 这里称“共工氏”，同样与颛顼争为帝，怒而撞向不周之山，折断天柱、断绝地维。
sections.bodyEn: Here he is called “Gonggong-shi”; again he contends with Zhuanxu for rulership and strikes Mount Buzhou in anger, breaking the pillar of heaven and snapping the cords of the earth.
sections.uncertaintyNote: “共工”与“共工氏”的称谓差异保留，不判定其为神祇、氏族首领或二者兼有。

sections.bodyEn: Heaven tilts to the northwest and the sun, moon and stars draw toward it; the earth falls short in the southeast, so all rivers and flood waters flow there. The wording differs slightly from “Tian Wen”.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 措辞差异只在对读中标注，不改写任一见证。

stories.canonicalTitle: Churning of the Ocean — Mahābhārata critical edition and Bhāgavata Purāṇa witnesses
stories.titleZh: 乳海搅拌：《摩诃婆罗多》精校本与《薄伽梵往世书》
stories.summaryZh: 两份梵语见证都以曼陀罗山为搅棒、婆苏吉为搅绳，并让檀文陀利捧着甘露出现、罗睺被神盘斩首；但托山的龟在精校本中是龟王阿库帕拉，在《薄伽梵往世书》中是毗湿奴的龟形化身，湿婆饮毒也只见于后者的当前定位。吴哥寺浮雕继续作为独立的物质见证。
stories.summaryEn: Both Sanskrit witnesses use Mount Mandara as the rod and Vāsuki as the rope, have Dhanvantari emerge with the amṛta and Rāhu beheaded by the discus; but the tortoise supporting the mountain is the tortoise king Akūpāra in the critical edition and Viṣṇu's tortoise form in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, and Śiva drinking the poison appears only at the latter's locator. The Angkor Wat relief remains a separate material witness.
stories.editorialNote: 精校本正文与往世书分开对读；“未陈述”不等于所有写本都没有。现代虔信译本不复制，神学解释不作裁定。

conflicts.summary: The Mahābhārata critical edition (Ādiparvan 1.16) has the tortoise king Akūpāra bear Mount Mandara, while the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (8.7) has Viṣṇu himself assume a tortoise form to raise it.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain both as coexisting textual witnesses. Akūpāra and Kūrma remain separate entities; no identity claim is made without an explicit source-backed identification.
conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Mahābhārata critical-edition witness the tortoise king Akūpāra bears Mount Mandara during the churning.
conflicts.claimBStatement: In the Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness Viṣṇu, in the form of a giant tortoise, raises Mount Mandara on his back.
conflicts.storyNotes: v0.30 witness comparison; Akūpāra and Kūrma are not equated.

witnessComparisons.editorialNoteZh: 两份见证对拔山者的叙述不同；均为中等置信度，待逐颂校对。
witnessComparisons.editorialNoteEn: The witnesses differ on who uproots the mountain; both rows are medium confidence pending verse-level collation.

sections.bodyZh: 精校本《初篇》1.15 中，诸神聚集在须弥山上商议如何得到甘露；那罗延（毗湿奴）建议诸神与阿修罗一起搅动大海。
sections.bodyEn: In the critical edition at Ādiparvan 1.15, the gods gather on Mount Meru to deliberate how to obtain the amṛta; Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) advises that gods and asuras churn the ocean together.
sections.uncertaintyNote: “那罗延”在此按既有毗湿奴实体连接，不扩展神学解释。

sections.headingZh: 曼陀罗山、婆苏吉与龟王
sections.headingEn: Mandara, Vāsuki and the tortoise king
sections.bodyZh: 巨蛇阿难陀拔起曼陀罗山作为搅棒，龙王婆苏吉充当搅绳；山的底部由龟王阿库帕拉承托。这一见证没有说龟王是毗湿奴的化身。
sections.bodyEn: The serpent Ananta uproots Mount Mandara to serve as the churning rod and the nāga Vāsuki serves as the rope; the tortoise king Akūpāra bears the base of the mountain. This witness does not say that the tortoise king is a form of Viṣṇu.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 阿难陀拔山一项为中等置信度，待逐颂校对；阿难陀尚未单独建实体。

sections.headingZh: 檀文陀利捧着甘露出现
sections.bodyZh: 搅拌中先后涌现多种存在与宝物，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
sections.bodyEn: As the churning goes on, a series of beings and treasures emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不从其他版本补齐。

sections.headingEn: The deluding female form and Rāhu
sections.bodyZh: 阿修罗夺走甘露后，那罗延化作迷惑人的女子形象，把甘露取回交给诸神。罗睺假扮天神偷饮甘露，被日月揭发后，那罗延以神盘斩下其头；随后天神与阿修罗爆发大战。
sections.bodyEn: After the Dānavas seize the amṛta, Nārāyaṇa takes on a deluding female form and recovers it for the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, drinks some of it; when the Sun and Moon expose him, Nārāyaṇa cuts off his head with the discus, and a great battle between gods and Dānavas follows.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 专名实体“摩希尼”只连接《薄伽梵往世书》见证；此处保留“迷惑的女身”描述。

sections.headingEn: Scope of the constituted critical text
sections.bodyZh: 在精校本 1.15–1.17 的正文里，没有湿婆吞下毒药的情节。这只说明本定位“未陈述”，不代表所有写本或地方传统都没有；校勘记录与附录尚待逐项核对。
sections.bodyEn: The constituted critical text at 1.15–1.17 does not include Śiva swallowing the poison. This records only that the locator does not state it; it does not mean that every manuscript or regional tradition lacks it, and the apparatus and appendices still have to be checked.
sections.evidenceNote: 精校本初篇 1.15–1.17 正文范围与 BORI 精校本说明。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 写本校勘与附录已作为独立研究队列排队。

sections.headingZh: 诸神与阿修罗暂时结盟
sections.headingEn: A truce between gods and asuras
sections.bodyZh: 《薄伽梵往世书》第八篇第5–6章中，诸神按毗湿奴的建议与阿修罗暂时结盟，合力拔起曼陀罗山并运往大海，毗湿奴亲自出手相助。
sections.bodyEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5–8.6, on Viṣṇu's advice the gods make a temporary truce with the asuras; together they uproot Mount Mandara and carry it toward the ocean, with Viṣṇu himself stepping in to help.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 运山过程的细节只作概述，待逐颂校对。

sections.headingEn: Viṣṇu takes the form of a tortoise
sections.bodyZh: 以婆苏吉为绳开始搅拌后，曼陀罗山沉入水中；毗湿奴化作巨龟潜到山下，用背托起大山。
sections.bodyEn: Once the churning begins with Vāsuki as the rope, Mount Mandara sinks into the water; Viṣṇu assumes the form of a giant tortoise, dives beneath it and raises the mountain on his back.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 与精校本的龟王阿库帕拉构成显式见证差异，不做身份等同。

sections.bodyZh: 搅拌最先产生可怕的毒药，向各方蔓延；众生求助于湿婆，湿婆把毒药饮下。
sections.bodyEn: The churning first produces a terrible poison that spreads in every direction; beings turn to Śiva, who drinks it.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 后续图像传统与虔信解释未在本批次逐句建模。

sections.bodyZh: 其后又涌现多种宝物与存在，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
sections.bodyEn: A series of treasures and beings then emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不与精校本合并。

sections.bodyZh: 阿修罗抢走甘露后，毗湿奴化身为摩希尼迷惑他们，并把甘露分给诸神。罗睺假扮天神混入其中饮下甘露，被日月指认后，毗湿奴以神盘斩下其头。
sections.bodyEn: When the asuras snatch the amṛta, Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī, captivates them and distributes the amṛta to the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, slips in and drinks; when the Sun and Moon point him out, Viṣṇu severs his head with the discus.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 罗睺后来的天体身份不在本批次建模。

stories.canonicalTitle: From Atum to Horus — a family of Egyptian gods
stories.titleZh: 从阿图姆到荷鲁斯：埃及众神的一家
stories.summaryZh: UCL 数字埃及把零散的古代文献整理成一个神族谱系：太阳神阿图姆生出舒与泰芙努特，他们又生出大地之神盖布与天空女神努特；舒把天地分开。后来塞特杀害兄弟奥西里斯，伊西斯收集遗体并怀上荷鲁斯。这是一份学术综述，不是某一部古代文献的原文顺序。
stories.summaryEn: UCL Digital Egypt orders scattered ancient references into one divine family: the sun-god Atum brings forth Shu and Tefnet, who produce Geb (earth) and Nut (sky); Shu holds them apart. Later Seth murders his brother Osiris, and Isis gathers the body and conceives Horus. It is a scholarly synthesis, not the sequence of a single ancient text.
stories.editorialNote: 学术综述层；古代文本见证尚未逐条拆分，各神亲属关系以 UCL 页面的表述为准。

versions.narrativeScope: 阿图姆的子女、天地分离与奥西里斯故事的概要
versions.rightsNote: 只发布定位与独立概述。

sections.bodyZh: 在埃及的创世观念里，主要的创造者是太阳神，他也被称为阿图姆。他最先生出一男一女：舒和泰芙努特。学者认为“舒”这个名字和“干燥”有关，“泰芙努特”则代表湿润。
sections.bodyEn: In Egyptian creation thought the principal creator is the sun-god, also called Atum. His first offshoots are a son and a daughter, Shu and Tefnet; scholars link Shu's name to dryness and read Tefnet as moisture.
sections.evidenceNote: UCL Digital Egypt 创世页面。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “干燥／湿润”是现代学者的词源解释。

sections.bodyZh: 舒和泰芙努特又生下两个孩子：大地之神盖布和天空女神努特。干燥与湿润，变成了坚实的大地和古埃及人眼中充满水的天空。
sections.bodyEn: Shu and Tefnet in turn produce two children: Geb, god of the earth, and Nut, goddess of the sky — dryness and moisture crystallised into solid earth and a sky the Egyptians thought of as watery.

sections.headingEn: Shu holds earth and sky apart
sections.bodyZh: 盖布和努特被舒分开，天在上、地在下。零散的古代记载暗示，这种分离必须被强制维持，否则天地还会继续生出神来。
sections.bodyEn: Shu separates Geb and Nut, sky above and earth below. Scattered references suggest the separation had to be enforced, or earth and sky would keep producing divine offspring.
sections.evidenceNote: UCL 页面关于天地分离的说明。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是学者对零散材料的归纳，不是单一文本的原话。

sections.headingZh: 塞特、奥西里斯与伊西斯
sections.bodyZh: 后来，奥西里斯“无序的兄弟”塞特出于嫉妒杀害了他，把遗体分开，并取代他成为世界之王。伊西斯找回奥西里斯的肢体，让遗体恢复到足以受孕，生下了荷鲁斯。
sections.bodyEn: Later Osiris's anarchic brother Seth, out of jealousy, murders him, dismembers him and takes his place as king of the world. Isis collects the limbs and revives the body enough to conceive a child, Horus.

stories.canonicalTitle: The Eye of Ra becomes Sekhmet — Tale of the Heavenly Cow
stories.titleZh: 拉的眼睛化作塞赫麦特：天牛之书
stories.summaryZh: 人类反叛太阳神拉。拉把自己的“眼睛”派出去惩罚人类，她化作塞赫麦特，几乎把人类消灭。众神把一湖啤酒染成血红色，她喝醉后恢复成慈爱的哈托尔。
stories.summaryEn: Humankind rebels against the sun-god Ra. He sends out his Eye to punish them; as Sekhmet she almost wipes humanity out, until the gods dye a lake of beer blood-red and she drinks, growing gentle again as Hathor.
stories.editorialNote: 依据 UCL 对新王国宗教文献《天牛之书》的概述；塞赫麦特与哈托尔在数据库中仍是两个实体。

sections.bodyZh: 一部新王国时期的宗教文献记载：人们起来反叛太阳神拉。拉决定惩罚他们，后来他也离开人间，退到天上。
sections.bodyEn: A New Kingdom religious composition records that people rebel against the sun-god Ra. He resolves to punish them, and in the end he withdraws to the sky.
sections.evidenceNote: UCL 页面对《天牛之书》的概述。

sections.bodyZh: 拉把自己的眼睛从身体里派出去，成为一个独立的“女儿”。她化作塞赫麦特——意思是“强大的女神”——几乎把人类全部消灭。
sections.bodyEn: Ra sends his Eye out from his body as a separate offshoot, a 'daughter'. As Sekhmet, 'the mighty goddess', she almost annihilates humankind.
sections.evidenceNote: 同一概述的“拉的眼睛”段落。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “强大的女神”是 UCL 给出的释义。

sections.bodyZh: 众神用计：他们把一湖啤酒染成红色，看起来像人血。她喝下后醉得香甜，脾气也软化下来，重新变回慈爱、温柔的哈托尔。
sections.bodyEn: The gods play a trick: they colour a lake of beer red to look like human blood. She drinks, becomes sweetly drunk, and reverts to her loving, maternal character as Hathor.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是故事中的性格转变；数据库不把两位女神合并为同一实体。

stories.canonicalTitle: Weighing the heart — Anubis and Thoth in the Papyrus of Ani
stories.titleZh: 称量心脏：阿尼纸草中的阿努比斯与托特
stories.summaryZh: 大英博物馆藏《阿尼纸草》第3框画着审判大厅：天平一边放着阿尼的心脏，另一边是代表玛阿特的羽毛。胡狼头的阿努比斯扶稳天平，托特既以狒狒形象坐在天平上，又以朱鹭头书吏的形象准备记录结果。
stories.summaryEn: British Museum Papyrus of Ani, frame 3, shows the Hall of Judgment: Ani's heart in one pan, a feather representing Maat in the other. Jackal-headed Anubis steadies the balance, and Thoth appears both as a baboon on top of it and as the ibis-headed scribe ready to record the result.
stories.editorialNote: 依据博物馆对单件纸草画面的描述；结果判定与怪兽阿米特未在本框记录中出现，不补写。

sections.bodyZh: 画面中央是一座天平。左边的秤盘里放着阿尼的心脏，右边是一根羽毛，代表真理与秩序女神玛阿特。
sections.bodyEn: At the centre stands a balance. In the left pan lies Ani's heart; in the right, a feather representing Maat, goddess of truth and order.
sections.evidenceNote: 大英博物馆 EA10470,3 藏品描述。

sections.bodyZh: 胡狼头的阿努比斯跪在天平旁，拉着右边秤盘的绳子，扶稳天平的铅锤。博物馆的说明称他是“在防腐之所的那一位”。
sections.bodyEn: Jackal-headed Anubis kneels by the balance, holding the cord of the right-hand pan and steadying its plumb bob. The museum describes him as 'he who is in the place of embalming'.
sections.evidenceNote: 同一藏品描述中关于阿努比斯的部分。

sections.bodyZh: 托特在画中出现两次：一只小狒狒坐在天平顶端；右边站着朱鹭头的“众神书吏”，手持调色板和芦苇笔，准备记下审问的结果。
sections.bodyEn: Thoth appears twice: as a small baboon sitting on top of the balance, and as the ibis-headed scribe of the gods standing to the right with palette and reed, ready to write down the result.
sections.evidenceNote: 同一藏品描述中关于托特的部分。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 称量的最终结果和吞噬心脏的怪兽不在这条博物馆描述里，本站不补写。

stories.canonicalTitle: Two mourning goddesses — Isis and Nephthys
stories.titleZh: 两位哀悼的女神：伊西斯与奈芙蒂斯
stories.summaryZh: 大都会艺术博物馆的一对托勒密时期木像：奈芙蒂斯跪着，举手掩面哀悼；另一尊是同样姿势的伊西斯。博物馆说明，在古埃及的图像中，这两位女神常守在奥西里斯遗体的两侧。

stories.canonicalTitle: Izanagi and Izanami — making the land, Yomi and purification
stories.titleZh: 伊邪那岐与伊邪那美：造岛、黄泉与禊祓
stories.summaryZh: 天神命伊邪那岐与伊邪那美巩固漂浮的大地。两神站在天浮桥上，用天沼矛搅动海水，滴下的盐水堆成淤能碁吕岛。伊邪那美生下火神后被烧伤而死；伊邪那岐追到黄泉，她却说已经吃了黄泉的食物。伊邪那岐回来后洗净身体，最后从左眼、右眼和鼻子生出天照大神、月读和须佐之男。
stories.summaryEn: The heavenly deities command Izanagi and Izanami to consolidate the drifting land. From the Floating Bridge of Heaven they stir the brine with a jewelled spear, and the drops become Onogoro Island. Izanami dies after bearing the fire deity; Izanagi follows her to Yomi, but she has already eaten of its hearth. Returning, he purifies himself, and from his left eye, right eye and nose are born Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi and Susanoo.
stories.editorialNote: 依据张伯伦 1882 年英译《古事记》的第三至第十节；《日本书纪》的不同说法另行保存，不合并。

sections.headingEn: A spear from the Floating Bridge
sections.bodyZh: 天上的众神命令伊邪那岐和伊邪那美去巩固还在漂浮的大地，并交给他们一支镶玉的天沼矛。两神站在天浮桥上，把矛伸进海里搅动；提起矛时，矛尖滴下的盐水层层堆积，成了淤能碁吕岛。
sections.bodyEn: The heavenly deities command Izanagi and Izanami to make firm the drifting land and give them a jewelled spear. Standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, they stir the brine; when they lift the spear, the drops from its tip pile up into Onogoro Island.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 《日本书纪》说两神是自己决定动手，本版不合并。

sections.headingEn: The birth of the fire deity
sections.bodyZh: 两神结合，生出许多岛屿和神灵。可是伊邪那美生下火神时被烧伤，病倒在床，最终“神去”——也就是死去。
sections.bodyEn: Joined together, the pair bring forth islands and deities. But when Izanami gives birth to the Deity-of-Fire she is burned, falls sick, and at length 'divinely retires' — she dies.

sections.bodyZh: 伊邪那岐想再见到妻子，便追到黄泉，请她回去：“我们造的国土还没有完成。”伊邪那美回答：你来得太晚了，我已经吃了黄泉灶火煮的东西——不过她答应去和黄泉的神商量。
sections.bodyEn: Longing to see her, Izanagi follows Izanami to Yomi and asks her to come back, for the lands they made are not yet finished. She answers that he has come too late: she has already eaten from the hearth of Yomi — yet she agrees to consult the deities there.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 之后的逃离情节可参看本库“黄泉中的八雷神”故事。

sections.bodyZh: 伊邪那岐回来后在水中洗净自己，身上不断化生出神。最后，他洗左眼时生出天照大神，洗右眼时生出月读，洗鼻子时生出须佐之男。
sections.bodyEn: Back from Yomi, Izanagi bathes to purify himself, and deities are born as he washes. Last of all, washing his left eye brings forth Amaterasu, his right eye Tsukuyomi, and his nose Susanoo.
sections.evidenceNote: 张伯伦译本第十节（kj017）及译注。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 三神的通行名称来自译者注释。

The deity born when Izanagi washes his right eye is rendered by Chamberlain as His Augustness Moon-Night-Possessor.
The deity born when Izanagi washes his left eye is rendered by Chamberlain as Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.
The heavenly deities command Izanagi and Izanami to make and consolidate the drifting land and grant them a heavenly jewelled spear.
Deities are born as Izanagi bathes to purify himself after Yomi.
Izanami stands with Izanagi on the Floating Bridge of Heaven while the brine is stirred.
Izanami answers that he came too late, for she has already eaten of the hearth of Yomi, though she will consult the deities there.
Izanami gives birth to the Deity-of-Fire.
The deity born when Izanagi washes his nose is rendered by Chamberlain as His Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness.

stories.canonicalTitle: Njörðr, Freyr and Freyja — the Vanir family
stories.titleZh: 华纳神族：尼奥尔德、弗雷与芙蕾雅
stories.summaryZh: 尼奥尔德住在诺欧通，掌管风和海，原本在华纳海姆长大，作为人质来到阿萨神族。他的儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和丰收；女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每次出征都分走一半战死者，乘坐两只猫拉的车。弗雷后来为了娶葛德，交出了自己的宝剑。
stories.summaryEn: Njörðr lives at Nóatún and rules wind and sea; raised in Vanaheim, he came to the Æsir as a hostage. His son Freyr rules rain, sunshine and harvests; his daughter Freyja lives at Fólkvangr, takes half the slain and drives a chariot pulled by two cats. Later Freyr gives away his sword to win Gerðr.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第23、24、37章；诗体埃达中的对应诗篇另行登记。

sections.bodyZh: 尼奥尔德住在天上一个叫诺欧通的地方。他掌管风的运行，能平息海浪和火焰；出海航行和捕鱼的人都向他祈祷。他在华纳海姆长大，后来作为人质被送到阿萨神族。
sections.bodyEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún. He rules the motion of the wind and can calm sea and fire; those who sail or fish pray to him. He was raised in Vanaheim and later given to the Æsir as a hostage.

sections.bodyZh: 尼奥尔德有一儿一女。儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和大地的收成，人们向他祈求丰年与富足。女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每当她骑马出战，就分得一半战死者，另一半归奥丁；她乘坐的车由两只猫拉着。
sections.bodyEn: Njörðr has a son and a daughter. Freyr rules rain, sunshine and the produce of the earth, and people pray to him for good seasons and wealth. Freyja lives at Fólkvangr; whenever she rides to battle she takes half the slain, Odin the other half, and her chariot is drawn by two cats.

sections.bodyZh: 后来，弗雷爱上了巨人之女葛德。为了娶到她，他把自己的宝剑交给了别人作为代价——这把剑从此不在他手中。
sections.bodyEn: Later Freyr falls in love with Gerðr, a giant's daughter. To win her he gives away his sword as the price, and the sword is no longer his.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 葛德尚未单独建立实体；诸神黄昏中的后果另行登记。

stories.canonicalTitle: Týr's hand and the binding of Fenrir
stories.titleZh: 提尔的手：束缚芬里尔
stories.summaryZh: 提尔是众神中最勇敢的一位。众神要捆住越长越大的狼芬里尔，狼要求有人把手放进它嘴里作担保。只有提尔伸出了右手；当狼发现自己挣脱不开，就咬断了他的手。所以提尔只有一只手。
stories.summaryEn: Týr is the boldest of the gods. When they set out to bind the growing wolf Fenrir, the wolf demands a hand in its mouth as a pledge. Only Týr offers his right hand; when the wolf finds it cannot break free, it bites the hand off — and so Týr is one-handed.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第25、34章；芬里尔在诸神黄昏中的结局见既有故事。

sections.bodyZh: 斯诺里说，提尔是众神中最勇敢、最无畏的一位，打仗时人们向他祈求胜利。他只有一只手。
sections.bodyEn: Snorri says Týr is the boldest and most valiant of the gods, invoked for victory in battle — and he has only one hand.

sections.bodyZh: 众神想用一条魔法绳索捆住狼芬里尔。狼起了疑心，要求有人把手放进它嘴里，保证这不是诡计。众神面面相觑，只有提尔伸出了右手。
sections.bodyEn: The gods mean to bind the wolf Fenrir with a magic fetter. Suspicious, the wolf demands that someone put a hand in its mouth as a pledge of good faith. Only Týr holds out his right hand.

sections.bodyZh: 绳索越挣越紧，狼发现自己被骗了，便咬断了提尔的手。众神都笑了，只有提尔没有笑。
sections.bodyEn: The more the wolf struggles, the tighter the fetter grows. Realizing it has been tricked, Fenrir bites off Týr's hand — and all the gods laugh, except Týr.

stories.canonicalTitle: Heimdallr, watchman of the gods
stories.titleZh: 海姆达尔：众神的守望者
stories.summaryZh: 海姆达尔住在彩虹桥边的希敏约格，替众神守着桥，防备山巨人。他睡得比鸟还少，夜里能看见一百里远，连草和羊毛生长的声音都听得见。他有一支加拉尔号角，吹响时所有世界都能听到。人们还说他是九位姐妹母亲的儿子。
stories.summaryEn: Heimdallr lives at Himinbjörg beside the rainbow bridge Bifröst and guards it for the gods against the mountain-giants. He needs less sleep than a bird, sees a hundred leagues by night, and hears grass and wool growing. His horn Gjallarhorn can be heard in all worlds, and he is called the son of nine mothers who were sisters.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第27章。

stories.canonicalTitle: Ymir and the shaping of the world
stories.titleZh: 尤弥尔与世界的形成
stories.summaryZh: 太初有一道深渊，北方的寒霜遇到南方的热气，化出巨人尤弥尔。后来奥丁和他的兄弟维利、维杀死了尤弥尔，用他的身体造出世界：肉成了大地，血成了海洋和湖泊，骨头成了山石，头骨成了天空。
stories.summaryEn: In the beginning there is a great void where rime from the north meets heat from the south, and from it the giant Ymir arises. Later Odin and his brothers Vili and Vé kill Ymir and build the world from his body: his flesh becomes the earth, his blood the sea and lakes, his bones the rocks, his skull the sky.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第5–8章；《女巫的预言》等诗歌见证另行对读。

stories.canonicalTitle: Frigg's oaths and the death of Baldr
stories.titleZh: 弗丽嘉的誓言与巴德尔之死
stories.summaryZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子，知道一切命运。她的儿子巴德尔梦见自己有危险，她便让火、水、金属、石头、草木和野兽都发誓不伤害他——唯独漏掉了一株幼小的槲寄生。巴德尔最后正是被槲寄生杀死的。
stories.summaryEn: Frigg, Odin's wife, knows all fates. When her son Baldr dreams of danger, she makes fire, water, metals, stones, plants and beasts swear not to harm him — all except a young shoot of mistletoe. In the end it is mistletoe that kills Baldr.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第20、49章；之后的冥界求情与报复情节尚未逐段登记。

sections.headingEn: The goddess who knows all fates
sections.bodyZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子。斯诺里说，她知道一切人的命运，只是从不说出来。
sections.bodyEn: Frigg is Odin's wife. Snorri says she knows the fates of all, though she does not speak them aloud.

sections.bodyZh: 巴德尔做了不祥的梦。弗丽嘉便去找火、水、铁和各种金属、石头、土地、树木、疾病、野兽、鸟和蛇，让它们都发誓不伤害巴德尔。只有长在英灵殿西边的一株小槲寄生，她觉得太小，没有让它发誓。
sections.bodyEn: Baldr has ominous dreams, so Frigg makes fire, water, iron and all metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds and serpents swear not to harm him. Only a young mistletoe shoot she thinks too small to ask.

sections.bodyZh: 众神以为巴德尔刀枪不入，便拿东西扔他取乐。然而那株没有发誓的槲寄生被做成了投枪，巴德尔被它刺中而死。
sections.bodyEn: Believing Baldr unharmable, the gods amuse themselves by throwing things at him. But the mistletoe that never swore is made into a dart, and Baldr is struck down and dies.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 投掷者与幕后之人的情节将在后续批次逐段登记。

stories.canonicalTitle: The birth of Huitzilopochtli on Serpent Mountain
stories.titleZh: 蛇山上的诞生：维齐洛波奇特利
stories.summaryZh: 科阿特利库埃在蛇山打扫时，一团羽毛飘落，她把它塞在腰间，因此怀孕。女儿科约尔沙乌基认为这是耻辱，带着四百个兄弟要杀死母亲。就在他们冲上山顶时，维齐洛波奇特利全副武装地出生，砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，把兄弟们赶散。
stories.summaryEn: While sweeping on Coatepec, Coatlicue picks up a ball of feathers, tucks it at her waist and conceives. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui, shamed, leads the four hundred brothers to kill their mother. As they reach the summit, Huitzilopochtli is born fully armed, beheads Coyolxauhqui and scatters the brothers.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章（萨阿贡编纂，16世纪）；学者把这段故事与大神庙布局相联系属于解释层。

sections.bodyZh: 科阿特利库埃住在蛇山上。一天她打扫时，一团羽毛从天上飘下来。她把羽毛捡起来，塞在腰间——就这样怀孕了。
sections.bodyEn: Coatlicue lives on Coatepec. One day as she sweeps, a ball of feathers drifts down. She picks it up and tucks it at her waist — and so she becomes pregnant.
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyZh: 她的女儿科约尔沙乌基对兄弟们——四百个南方人——说：母亲让我们蒙羞，我们必须杀了她。于是他们全副武装，朝蛇山进发。
sections.bodyEn: Her daughter Coyolxauhqui tells her brothers, the four hundred Centzon Huitznahua, that their mother has shamed them and must be killed. Armed, they set out for Coatepec.
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyZh: 腹中的维齐洛波奇特利安慰母亲：不要怕，我知道该怎么做。敌人冲上山顶的那一刻，他出生了，手持盾牌、投枪和投枪器。
sections.bodyEn: From the womb Huitzilopochtli comforts his mother: do not be afraid, I know what to do. The moment the attackers reach the summit he is born, carrying shield, darts and dart-thrower.
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyZh: 维齐洛波奇特利砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，她的身体沿着蛇山滚落下去。四百个兄弟也被他从山顶追得四散奔逃。
sections.bodyEn: Huitzilopochtli cuts off Coyolxauhqui's head, and her body tumbles down the side of Coatepec. He drives the four hundred brothers from the summit, scattering them in every direction.
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 学者认为这段叙事与大神庙的布局相呼应，属于解释，不写成事实。

stories.canonicalTitle: Quetzalcoatl and Titlacauan at Tollan
stories.titleZh: 图拉的羽蛇神与蒂特拉卡瓦
stories.summaryZh: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷讲述图拉的大法师羽蛇神。巫师们来到他身边，其中一位叫蒂特拉卡瓦，也就是特斯卡特利波卡；他们带来的种种征兆让羽蛇神的荣光走向终结。羽蛇神离开时，随行的人在两座雪山之间冻死。
stories.summaryEn: Florentine Codex Book 3 tells of Quetzalcoatl, a great wizard at Tollan. Sorcerers come to him — among them Titlacauan, also called Tezcatlipoca — and their portents bring his glory to an end. As he departs, his followers freeze to death between two snow-capped volcanoes.
stories.editorialNote: 依据第三卷第2–5、14章的章节标题与概要；各章细节尚未逐段建模。

sections.headingZh: 被当作神的蒂特拉卡瓦
sections.headingEn: Titlacauan, held to be a god
sections.bodyZh: 第三卷第2章讲人们怎样把一位叫蒂特拉卡瓦、也叫特斯卡特利波卡的人物当作神来敬奉。
sections.bodyEn: Chapter 2 of Book 3 tells how one called Titlacauan, or Tezcatlipoca, came to be regarded as a god.
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第2章。

sections.bodyZh: 第3章讲羽蛇神——图拉的一位大法师。第4章说，当巫师们来到他身边，他的荣光便走到了尽头；第5章又记下蒂特拉卡瓦带来的另一个异兆。
sections.bodyEn: Chapter 3 tells of Quetzalcoatl, a great wizard at Tollan. Chapter 4 relates how his glory came to an end when the sorcerers came to him, and chapter 5 records another portent brought about by Titlacauan.
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第3–5章。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 本段依据章节标题与概要，具体情节尚未逐句核对。

sections.bodyZh: 第14章记载，羽蛇神离去时，追随他的人经过伊斯塔克特佩特尔与波波卡特佩特尔两座雪山之间，被冻死在冰雪里。
sections.bodyEn: Chapter 14 records that as Quetzalcoatl departs, his vassals freeze to death in the ice as they pass between Iztactepetl and Popocatepetl.
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第14章。

stories.canonicalTitle: Two gods on one pyramid — the Templo Mayor
stories.titleZh: 一座金字塔上的两位神：大神庙
stories.summaryZh: 特诺奇蒂特兰的大神庙顶上并立着两座神殿：南边供奉太阳战神、墨西加人的守护神维齐洛波奇特利，北边供奉与农业相连的雨神特拉洛克。墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所说，神庙始建于1325年，此后多次重建与扩建。
stories.summaryEn: Atop the Templo Mayor of Tenochtitlan stood two shrines: on the south, Huitzilopochtli, solar god of war and patron of the Mexica; on the north, Tlaloc, god of rain linked to agriculture. INAH says the first small temple was built at the city's founding in 1325 and was rebuilt and enlarged many times.

sections.headingEn: The rain god on the north
sections.bodyZh: 北侧的神殿属于特拉洛克——掌管雨水、与农业紧密相连的神。战争与农业，两位神并立在同一座金字塔的顶端。
sections.bodyEn: The northern temple belongs to Tlaloc, god of rain and closely tied to agriculture. War and farming stand side by side at the top of one pyramid.
sections.evidenceNote: INAH 大神庙遗址博物馆说明。

stories.canonicalTitle: Three Maya gods in stone, clay and glyph
stories.titleZh: 石头、陶盘与文字中的三位玛雅神
stories.summaryZh: 三份独立见证，各讲一位玛雅神：奇琴伊察的卡斯蒂略金字塔又叫“库库尔坎神庙”；大都会博物馆的一只陶盘上，雨神恰克半身浸在水中；同一博物馆的展览介绍年老的天神伊察姆纳和他的鸟形化身。三份见证分开阅读，不拼成一个统一神话。
stories.summaryEn: Three separate witnesses, one god each: Chichen-Itza's El Castillo is also called the Temple of Kukulkan; a Met plate shows the rain god Chahk waist-deep in water; and a Met exhibition presents the aged sky god Itzamnaaj and his bird avatar. They are read separately, not stitched into one myth.
stories.editorialNote: 三个版本分别来自联合国教科文组织遗产记录与大都会艺术博物馆的两份说明；不把玛雅与墨西加的羽蛇神合并。

sections.bodyZh: 奇琴伊察是尤卡坦半岛上的前西班牙时期古城，已列入世界遗产名录。联合国教科文组织的记录把卡斯蒂略金字塔列为城市北部建筑群中的主要建筑。
sections.bodyEn: Chichen-Itza is a pre-Hispanic city on the Yucatán peninsula, inscribed on the World Heritage List. UNESCO's record names El Castillo among the chief buildings of the city's northern group.
sections.evidenceNote: 联合国教科文组织世界遗产 483 号记录。

sections.bodyZh: 奇琴伊察北区最重要的建筑是卡斯蒂略金字塔，联合国教科文组织的记录说，它又被称为“库库尔坎神庙”。
sections.bodyEn: The chief monument of Chichen-Itza's northern group is El Castillo, which UNESCO's record says is also known as the Temple of Kukulkan.
sections.evidenceNote: 联合国教科文组织世界遗产 483 号记录。

sections.bodyZh: 同一记录提到一种最常见的说法：图拉之王“一芦苇·托皮尔钦·羽蛇”占领了这座城市，而“库库尔坎”正是玛雅人对“羽蛇”这个名字的翻译。
sections.bodyEn: The same record cites the most common version: the King of Tula, Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl, took the city — and 'Kukulkan' is how the Maya translated his name.
sections.evidenceNote: 联合国教科文组织世界遗产 483 号记录。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是关于统治者名号的传统说法，不把玛雅与墨西加的神合并为同一实体。

sections.bodyZh: 2022 年的展览按“众神的一生”展开：从婴儿、壮年到老年。其中的老年之神叫伊察姆纳（Itzamnaaj），他还有一个鸟形化身，两者在太初神话中都很重要。
sections.bodyEn: The 2022 exhibition followed the gods through life — infancy, prime and old age. The aged god is Itzamnaaj, who has a bird avatar; both play important roles in primordial myths.

stories.canonicalTitle: Enki and Ninhursaĝa in Dilmun
stories.titleZh: 恩基与宁胡尔萨格：迪尔蒙的植物
stories.summaryZh: 故事从纯净的迪尔蒙开始。恩基吃掉了那里长出的植物，宁胡尔萨格怒而诅咒他，恩基因此病倒。后来宁胡尔萨格回心转意，为恩基身上每一处病痛生出一位神灵，把他治好。
stories.summaryEn: The story begins in pure Dilmun. Enki eats the plants that have grown there; Ninhursaĝa curses him in anger, and he falls ill. Later she relents and brings forth a deity for each ailing part of his body, healing him.

stories.titleZh: 月神南纳航向尼普尔
stories.summaryZh: 月神南纳想念父亲恩利尔的城市尼普尔，便装满一船礼物，沿河航行前往。到了尼普尔，恩利尔欢迎他，赐给他满船的丰饶，让他带回自己的城市乌尔。

stories.canonicalTitle: Utu helps Gilgameš set out against Ḫuwawa
stories.titleZh: 太阳神乌图与吉尔伽美什的远征
stories.summaryZh: 吉尔伽美什决定进山建立名声。伙伴恩奇都提醒他：山是太阳神乌图的事，得先告诉乌图。吉尔伽美什向乌图祈求，乌图接受了他的眼泪作为礼物，赐给他七位勇士做向导，去面对山中的守护者胡瓦瓦。
stories.summaryEn: Gilgameš resolves to make his name in the mountains. His companion Enkidu warns that the mountains are Utu's concern, so the sun god must be told. Gilgameš prays, and Utu accepts his tears as a gift and grants him seven warriors as guides to face Ḫuwawa, the guardian of the mountains.

stories.canonicalTitle: Fuxi makes the eight trigrams
stories.titleZh: 伏羲始作八卦
stories.summaryZh: 《周易·系辞下》说：古时包牺氏（伏羲）治理天下，他抬头观察天象，低头观察地理，看鸟兽身上的纹理和各地的物产，近取自身、远取万物，于是开始画出八卦；他又把绳子打结做成网，用来打猎捕鱼。
stories.summaryEn: The Xi Ci II says that when Baoxi (Fuxi) ruled in antiquity, he looked up at heaven and down at the earth, studied the markings of birds and beasts and the land, drew on his own body and on distant things, and first made the eight trigrams; he also knotted cords into nets for hunting and fishing.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《系辞下》第二章；“包牺即伏羲”采用传统注疏的读法。

sections.bodyZh: 《系辞下》讲古代圣人的发明，第一位就是包牺氏——后世通常写作伏羲。书里说，远古的时候，是他在治理天下。
sections.bodyEn: Xi Ci II lists the inventions of the ancient sages, and the first is Baoxi — usually written Fuxi in later texts. In remote antiquity, it says, he ruled all under heaven.
sections.uncertaintyNote: “包牺”即“伏羲”是传统注疏的读法。

sections.bodyZh: 他抬头观察天上的日月星辰，低头观察大地的形势；又细看鸟兽身上的花纹，看各地适合生长什么。近处，他从自己的身体取法；远处，他从万物取法。
sections.bodyEn: He looked up at the images in the sky and down at the patterns of the earth; he studied the markings of birds and beasts and what each land was suited for. Near at hand he drew on his own body, and far off on all things.

sections.bodyZh: 于是他开始画出八卦——八个由三条线组成的符号，用来通达神明的德性，把万物的情状分门别类。
sections.bodyEn: Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams — eight figures of three lines each — to communicate with spirit-like virtue and to sort the dispositions of the myriad things.
sections.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“于是始作八卦”。

sections.bodyZh: 他还把绳子打结，做成罗网，人们用它打猎、捕鱼。《系辞》接下来再讲神农等后来的圣人，这里只讲伏羲这一段。
sections.bodyEn: He also knotted cords into nets, which people used to hunt and fish. The Xi Ci then moves on to later sages such as Shennong; this retelling covers only Baoxi's part.
sections.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“作结绳而为罔罟”。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 后续圣人的发明不在本故事范围内。

stories.canonicalTitle: The Yellow Emperor and Chiyou at Zhuolu
stories.titleZh: 黄帝战蚩尤：涿鹿之战
stories.summaryZh: 《史记·五帝本纪》说：神农氏衰落，诸侯互相攻伐，轩辕操练军队征讨不服者。蚩尤最为暴虐，作乱不听帝命。轩辕征召诸侯之兵，在涿鹿的原野擒杀蚩尤，诸侯于是尊他为天子，这就是黄帝。
stories.summaryEn: The Shiji's Annals of the Five Emperors say that as Shennong's house declined and the lords fought one another, Xuanyuan trained troops. Chiyou, the most violent, rebelled against the ruler's command; Xuanyuan levied the lords' armies, captured and killed him in the wilds of Zhuolu, and was honoured as Son of Heaven — the Yellow Emperor.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《史记·五帝本纪》；司马迁以史笔叙述，本站只登记文本所述，不作历史真实性断言。

sections.bodyZh: 黄帝是少典的儿子，姓公孙，名轩辕。他那个时代，神农氏的统治衰落了，诸侯互相攻打、欺压百姓，神农氏却无力征讨。轩辕于是操练军队，去讨伐不肯朝贡的诸侯。
sections.bodyEn: The Yellow Emperor was the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan. In his time the rule of Shennong had declined; the lords attacked one another and oppressed the people, and Shennong could not punish them. So Xuanyuan trained troops to subdue the lords who would not pay tribute.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 此前轩辕与炎帝在阪泉的三次交战本故事未展开。

sections.bodyZh: 诸侯之中，蚩尤最为凶暴，没有人能制服他。蚩尤起来作乱，不听从帝王的命令。
sections.bodyEn: Among the lords Chiyou was the most violent, and no one could subdue him. Chiyou rose in rebellion and would not obey the ruler's command.
sections.evidenceNote: 《五帝本纪》“蚩尤作乱，不用帝命”。

sections.bodyZh: 轩辕征召各路诸侯的军队，在涿鹿的原野上与蚩尤交战，终于把蚩尤擒住并杀死。
sections.bodyEn: Xuanyuan called up the armies of the lords and fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, and at last captured and killed him.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 涿鹿不在本站映射为现代坐标。

sections.bodyZh: 诸侯们都尊奉轩辕为天子，取代了神农氏，这就是黄帝。
sections.bodyEn: The lords all honoured Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong: this was the Yellow Emperor.
sections.evidenceNote: 《五帝本纪》“诸侯咸尊轩辕为天子”。

events.summaryZh: 轩辕征召各路诸侯的军队，在涿鹿的原野上与蚩尤交战，终于把蚩尤擒住并杀死。
events.summaryEn: Xuanyuan called up the armies of the lords and fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, and at last captured and killed him.
events.uncertaintyNote: 涿鹿不在本站映射为现代坐标。

events.summaryZh: 诸侯们都尊奉轩辕为天子，取代了神农氏，这就是黄帝。
events.summaryEn: The lords all honoured Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong: this was the Yellow Emperor.

claims.statement: As the house of Shennong declines and the lords attack one another, Xuanyuan trains troops to punish those who do not bring tribute.
The Annals of the Five Emperors are the textual witness used for the Zhuolu episode.

The Shiji introduces the Yellow Emperor as the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan.
He finally captures and kills Chiyou (遂禽殺蚩尤).
The lords all honour Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong; this is the Yellow Emperor.
Chiyou is the opponent at Zhuolu.
The Yellow Emperor levies the lords' troops and fights Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu.

stories.canonicalTitle: Pangu between heaven and earth
stories.titleZh: 盘古开天地：《三五历纪》佚文
stories.summaryZh: 三国吴人徐整的《三五历纪》已经失传，只在后世类书中留有引文。《艺文类聚》卷一引它说：天地未分时混沌如鸡蛋，盘古生在其中；一万八千年后天地开辟，清者为天、浊者为地；天每天高一丈，地每天厚一丈，盘古每天长一丈，又过一万八千年，天极高、地极深、盘古极长。
stories.summaryEn: Xu Zheng's Sanwu liji is lost, surviving only in later encyclopedias. Yiwen leiju juan 1 quotes it: before heaven and earth parted, all was chaos like a hen's egg, and Pangu was born inside; after 18,000 years they opened, clear becoming heaven and murky becoming earth; each day heaven rose a zhang, earth thickened a zhang and Pangu grew a zhang, until after another 18,000 years heaven was highest, earth deepest and Pangu tallest.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《艺文类聚》卷一所引《三五历纪》，并以《太平御览》卷一的引文对照；盘古身体化生万物另见他书，不在此合并。

sections.bodyZh: 很久以前，天和地还没有分开，到处是一团混沌，样子像一个鸡蛋。盘古就生在这团混沌之中。
sections.bodyEn: Long ago heaven and earth were not yet apart; everything was one chaos shaped like a hen's egg, and Pangu was born inside it.
sections.evidenceNote: 《艺文类聚》卷一引《三五历纪》；《太平御览》卷一引文字句略异。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 原书已佚，只能依靠类书引文。

sections.bodyZh: 过了一万八千年，天地开辟：轻而清的阳气上升成为天，重而浊的阴气下沉成为地。盘古就在天地之间，一天之中变化九次，比天更神，比地更圣。
sections.bodyEn: After 18,000 years heaven and earth opened: the light, clear yang rose to become heaven, the heavy, murky yin sank to become earth. Pangu stood between them, changing nine times a day, more divine than heaven and wiser than earth.
sections.evidenceNote: 同一引文“阳清为天，阴浊为地”。

sections.bodyZh: 从此天每天升高一丈，地每天加厚一丈，盘古也每天长高一丈。这样又过了一万八千年，天高到了极点，地深到了极点，盘古也长到了极点。在这之后，才有了三皇。
sections.bodyEn: From then on heaven rose a zhang each day, earth grew a zhang thicker, and Pangu grew a zhang taller. After another 18,000 years heaven was as high as it could be, earth as deep, and Pangu as tall. Only after that came the Three Sovereigns.
sections.evidenceNote: 同一引文“天日高一丈……盘古日长一丈”。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “盘古垂死化身为日月山川”出自另一部书，本故事不合并。

events.summaryEn: After 18,000 years heaven and earth opened: the light, clear yang rose to become heaven, the heavy, murky yin sank to become earth.

claims.statement: This story uses only the Sanwu liji quotation; the motif of Pangu's dying body becoming sun, moon, rivers and mountains comes from a different text and is not merged here.
The Sanwu liji is lost; its Pangu passage is known through quotations in later encyclopedias such as Yiwen leiju juan 1 and Taiping yulan juan 1.
Before heaven and earth separate, all is chaos like a hen's egg, and Pangu is born within it.

Each day heaven rises one zhang, earth thickens one zhang and Pangu grows one zhang; after another 18,000 years heaven is extremely high, earth extremely deep and Pangu extremely tall. Only afterwards come the Three Sovereigns.
After 18,000 years heaven and earth open: the clear yang becomes heaven, the murky yin becomes earth, and Pangu is between them, changing nine times a day.

stories.canonicalTitle: Nezha against Sun Wukong (Journey to the West, ch. 4)
stories.titleZh: 哪吒大战孙悟空：《西游记》第四回
stories.summaryZh: 孙悟空嫌弼马温官小，回花果山自称齐天大圣。托塔李天王与哪吒三太子奉命捉拿。哪吒变出三头六臂，悟空也变三头六臂；悟空拔毫毛变出分身，真身绕到背后打中哪吒，哪吒负痛败走。
stories.summaryEn: Finding his stable post too lowly, Sun Wukong returns home and calls himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven. Heavenly King Li and his third son Nezha are sent to seize him. Nezha takes three heads and six arms; Wukong does the same, then turns a hair into a double and strikes Nezha from behind, and Nezha retreats in pain.
stories.editorialNote: 明代小说《西游记》属于后世文学接受层，不当作古代神话见证；哪吒闹海等故事出自其他作品，未在此合并。

sections.bodyZh: 孙悟空发现“弼马温”只是个看马的小官，一气之下回到花果山，自称“齐天大圣”。玉帝派托塔李天王和他的三太子哪吒，带领天兵前去捉拿。
sections.bodyEn: Discovering that his title merely made him a keeper of horses, Sun Wukong storms back to his mountain and calls himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven. The Jade Emperor sends Heavenly King Li, bearer of the pagoda, and his third son Nezha with the heavenly troops to seize him.

sections.bodyZh: 哪吒大喝一声，变成三头六臂，六只手各拿一件兵器打来。悟空见了，也变成三头六臂，把金箍棒一晃变成三条，六只手拿着架住。
sections.bodyEn: Nezha gives a shout and becomes a figure with three heads and six arms, a weapon in every hand. Wukong does the same: he shakes his staff into three and parries with six hands.

sections.bodyZh: 两人斗得难分难解。悟空拔下一根毫毛，变成自己的模样继续迎敌，真身却绕到哪吒背后打了一棒。哪吒负痛败走，回去禀报父王：这猴子神通广大。
sections.bodyEn: Neither can win. Wukong plucks a hair and turns it into a double of himself to keep fighting, while his true body circles behind Nezha and strikes. Nezha flees in pain and reports to his father that the monkey's powers are great.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是小说情节，属于后世文学层。

events.summaryZh: 哪吒大喝一声，变成三头六臂，六只手各拿一件兵器打来。
events.summaryEn: Nezha gives a shout and becomes a figure with three heads and six arms, a weapon in every hand.

events.summaryZh: 两人斗得难分难解。
events.summaryEn: Neither can win.

Wukong also takes three heads and six arms and turns his staff into three to parry.

stories.canonicalTitle: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired
stories.titleZh: 第二次马格图雷德之战：达格达、莫莉甘、布里格与鲁格
stories.summaryZh: 中世纪爱尔兰传说《第二次马格图雷德之战》：达格达拥有“没有人吃不饱”的大锅；“百艺之主”鲁格来到塔拉；萨温节时达格达在河边遇见莫莉甘；布里格为战死的儿子哀哭，是爱尔兰第一次听到哀歌；鲁格用投石击毁巴洛尔的毒眼；战后莫莉甘向全爱尔兰宣告胜利。
stories.summaryEn: The medieval Irish saga Cath Maige Tuired: the Dagda's cauldron leaves no one unsatisfied; Lug, master of all arts, comes to Tara; at Samain the Dagda meets the Morrígan by the river; Bríg keens for her slain son, the first keening in Ireland; Lug's sling stone drives Balor's deadly eye through his head; and the Morrígan proclaims the victory across Ireland.
stories.editorialNote: 依据 Elizabeth A. Gray 1982 年校译本（CELT T300010）的段落编号；译文受版权保护，只发布定位与独立概述。

sections.bodyZh: 达努神族带来了四件宝物，其中一件是从穆里亚斯城带来的达格达的大锅：凡是围着它吃饭的人，从没有一个是不饱足地离开的。
sections.bodyEn: The Túatha Dé Danann brought four treasures. One was the Dagda's cauldron from the city of Murias: no company that ate from it ever went away unsatisfied.

sections.headingEn: The master of all arts at Tara
sections.bodyZh: 鲁格来到塔拉的大门前，守门人问他会什么手艺。他报出一门又一门，而宫里每门手艺都已有人；最后他问：有没有一个人能同时精通所有这些？于是他以“百艺之主”的身份被请了进去。
sections.bodyEn: Lug comes to the door of Tara, and the doorkeeper asks what art he brings. He names one after another, and each already has a master within — until he asks whether anyone there has all of them at once. So he is admitted as the Samildánach, master of all arts.

sections.bodyZh: 萨温节前后，达格达在乌恩辛河边遇见一个女人正在洗东西，一只脚踩在南岸，一只脚踩在北岸。她就是莫莉甘。两人结合之后，她告诉达格达弗魔族将在哪里登陆，并许诺要取弗魔王因德赫的心血。
sections.bodyEn: Around Samain the Dagda meets a woman washing at the river Unshin, one foot on the southern bank and one on the northern. She is the Morrígan. After they unite she tells him where the Fomoire will land and promises to take the heart's blood of their king Indech.

sections.bodyZh: 布里格是达格达的女儿，她和布雷斯的儿子鲁阿丹被派去刺杀铁匠戈伊布纽，却被戈伊布纽杀死。布里格赶来为儿子哀哭，先是尖声恸哭，最后低声啜泣——这是爱尔兰第一次听到哀歌与哭泣。
sections.bodyEn: Rúadán, son of Bres and of Bríg the Dagda's daughter, is sent to kill the smith Goibniu and is killed instead. Bríg comes and keens for her son, shrieking first and weeping at the end — the first time keening and weeping were heard in Ireland.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 文本写作 Bríg；与数据库中“布里吉德”实体的对应依学界通行用法。

sections.bodyZh: 弗魔族勇士巴洛尔有一只毒眼，只在战场上睁开，要四个人用把手才能抬起眼皮。鲁格用投石一击，石头把那只眼睛从巴洛尔脑后打了出去，结果看见它的反而是他自己的军队。
sections.bodyEn: The Fomorian champion Balor has a deadly eye, opened only on the battlefield, its lid lifted by four men with a handle. Lug casts a sling stone that drives the eye out through the back of Balor's head, so that it is his own host that looks upon it.

sections.bodyZh: 战斗结束后，恩玛斯的女儿莫莉甘把这场大胜宣告给爱尔兰的王者高地、神丘里的众灵、各条大河与河口，然后又说出关于未来的预言。
sections.bodyEn: When the battle is won, the Morrígan, daughter of Ernmas, proclaims the great victory to the royal heights of Ireland, its síd-hosts, its chief waters and river-mouths — and then speaks prophecy.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 预言诗的内容未逐句建模。

claims.statement: Balor has a destructive eye that is opened only on the battlefield; four men lift its lid with a polished handle.
No company ever went away from the Dagda's cauldron unsatisfied.
Cath Maige Tuired is the textual witness for the second battle of Mag Tuired.
When Rúadán is killed, Bríg comes and keens for her son, first shrieking and then weeping: the first time keening and weeping were heard in Ireland.
Among the four treasures of the Túatha Dé Danann, the Dagda's cauldron was brought from Murias.
At Samain the Dagda meets the Morrígan washing at the Unshin, one foot on each bank; they unite, and she tells him where the Fomoire will land.
Lug casts a sling stone that drives Balor's eye through the back of his head, so that it is Balor's own host that looks upon it.
Arriving at Tara, Lug is admitted as the one who possesses every art at once: the Samildánach.
After the battle the Morrígan, daughter of Ernmas, proclaims the great victory to the royal heights of Ireland, its síd-hosts, chief waters and river-mouths, and then prophesies.
Rúadán is the son of Bres and of Bríg, the Dagda's daughter.
The Dagda takes part in the preparations and the battle.
Lug fights in the battle and faces Balor.
The Morrígan aids the Túatha Dé Danann and proclaims the victory.
The Morrígan promises to destroy the Fomorian king Indech, taking the blood of his heart and the kidneys of his valour.

stories.canonicalTitle: The idols on the Kyiv hill — Perun and Mokosh
stories.titleZh: 基辅山岗上的神像：佩伦与莫科什
stories.summaryZh: 《往年纪事》980 年条：弗拉基米尔在基辅宫殿外的山岗上立起神像——银头金须的木雕佩伦，还有霍尔斯、达日博格、斯特里博格、西马尔格尔和莫科什，人们向它们献祭。988 年他受洗后下令推倒神像，佩伦被绑在马尾上拖下山，丢进第聂伯河。
stories.summaryEn: The Primary Chronicle's annal for 980: Volodimer sets up idols on the hill outside his Kyiv palace — a wooden Perun with a silver head and golden moustache, then Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog, Simargl and Mokosh — and people make offerings to them. After his baptism in 988 he has them cast down; Perun is tied to a horse's tail, dragged down the hill and thrown into the Dnieper.
stories.editorialNote: 依据《往年纪事》980 与 988 年条；编年史由皈依后的基督教修士编写，对旧信仰的描述带有立场；莫科什在此只有名字。

sections.bodyZh: 《往年纪事》980 年条记载：弗拉基米尔开始在基辅独自为王，就在宫殿庭院外的山岗上立起一排神像。
sections.bodyEn: The Primary Chronicle's annal for 980 records that when Volodimer began to reign alone in Kyiv, he set up a row of idols on the hill outside the palace courtyard.

sections.bodyZh: 最前面的是佩伦：木头雕成，头是银的，胡须是金的。
sections.bodyEn: First stood Perun, carved of wood, with a silver head and a golden moustache.

sections.headingEn: Mokosh at the end of the list
sections.bodyZh: 接下来是霍尔斯、达日博格、斯特里博格、西马尔格尔，名单的最后一位是莫科什。人们向这些神像献上祭品。编年史只记下了莫科什的名字，没有说她掌管什么。
sections.bodyEn: Then came Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog and Simargl, and last on the list, Mokosh. People brought offerings to the idols. The chronicle records only Mokosh's name, not what she governed.

stories.canonicalTitle: Mithra of the wide pastures — the Mihr Yasht
stories.titleZh: 广阔牧场之主密特拉：《密赫尔颂》
stories.summaryZh: 阿维斯塔第十颂《密赫尔颂》：阿胡拉·马兹达说，他创造密特拉时，使他与自己同样值得祭祀和祈祷；对密特拉说谎、背弃契约的人会给整个国家带来死亡；密特拉有千只耳朵、万只眼睛，在不朽的快马太阳之前最先越过哈拉山。
stories.summaryEn: The Mihr Yasht, tenth hymn of the Avesta: Ahura Mazda says he made Mithra as worthy of sacrifice and prayer as himself; whoever lies to Mithra and breaks the contract brings death to the whole land; Mithra has a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes and is the first god to rise over Mount Hara, before the swift-horsed sun.
stories.editorialNote: 依据达梅斯特泰尔译本（avesta.org）第10颂第1、2、7、13节；现代学者对诗句的理解另有讨论。

sections.bodyZh: 颂歌一开头，阿胡拉·马兹达对查拉图斯特拉说：我创造广阔牧场之主密特拉时，使他与我自己一样，值得献祭、值得祈祷。
sections.bodyEn: The hymn opens with Ahura Mazda telling Zarathustra: when I created Mithra, lord of wide pastures, I made him as worthy of sacrifice and as worthy of prayer as myself.

sections.bodyZh: 对密特拉说谎、背弃契约的恶人，会给整个国家带来死亡。所以契约绝不可背弃——不论是与信徒订立的，还是与不信者订立的。
sections.bodyEn: The wretch who lies to Mithra, breaking the contract, brings death upon the whole land. So the contract must never be broken, whether made with one of the faithful or with an unbeliever.
sections.uncertaintyNote: “契约”是译者对 miθra 一词的理解，学界另有讨论。

sections.headingEn: A thousand ears, ten thousand eyes
sections.bodyZh: 颂歌赞美密特拉说真话，是集会中的首领；他有一千只耳朵，一万只眼睛，什么都瞒不过他。
sections.bodyEn: The hymn praises Mithra as truth-speaking, a chief in assemblies, with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes — nothing escapes him.

sections.bodyZh: 每天清晨，他是天上诸神中第一个越过哈拉山的，比不朽的、驾着快马的太阳还要早。
sections.bodyEn: Each morning he is the first of the heavenly gods to reach over Mount Hara, ahead of the undying, swift-horsed sun.

stories.canonicalTitle: Sixteen good lands and their plagues — Videvdad 1
stories.titleZh: 十六片良地与它们的灾祸：《万迪达德》第一章
stories.summaryZh: 《万迪达德》第一章：阿胡拉·马兹达创造了十六片良地，第一片是善河岱提亚旁的雅利安瓦伊贾；每创造一片，“全然是死亡”的安格拉·曼纽就造出一种灾祸与之对抗——第一片是河中之蛇和寒冬，第二片是蝗虫。
stories.summaryEn: Videvdad 1: Ahura Mazda makes sixteen good lands, the first being Airyana Vaejah by the good river Daitya; for each, Angra Mainyu, who is all death, counter-creates a plague — the serpent in the river and winter for the first, the locust for the second.
stories.editorialNote: 依据达梅斯特泰尔译本（avesta.org）第一章；译者认为这是伊朗的宗教地理，而不是迁徙记录。

sections.bodyZh: 阿胡拉·马兹达说：我所创造的良地中，第一片是雅利安瓦伊贾，在善河岱提亚旁边。
sections.bodyEn: Ahura Mazda says: the first of the good lands I created was Airyana Vaejah, by the good river Daitya.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 雅利安瓦伊贾不映射为现代坐标。

sections.headingEn: The one who is all death
sections.bodyZh: 随后，“全然是死亡”的安格拉·曼纽来了，他针对这片良地造出了河中之蛇和寒冬，那是恶魔们的作品。
sections.bodyEn: Then came Angra Mainyu, who is all death, and against it he counter-created the serpent in the river and winter, a work of the daevas.

sections.bodyZh: 名单一片接一片地继续：第二片是粟特人居住的平原，安格拉·曼纽就造出蝗虫。如此一共列出十六片良地，每一片都对应一种反创造的灾祸。
sections.bodyEn: The list goes on land by land: the second is the plain where the Sughdhas dwell, and Angra Mainyu makes the locust. In all, sixteen good lands are named, each answered by a counter-created plague.
sections.evidenceNote: 第一章第二片良地及以下。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 译者认为这是宗教地理，混合了神话之地与真实国家；只有部分地名可以确认。

The list continues land by land — the second, the plains of the Sughdhas, is answered by the locust — until sixteen lands and sixteen plagues are named.
Ahura Mazda makes the sixteen good lands.
Angra Mainyu sets a counter-creation against each land.
Throughout Videvdad 1 every good land made by Ahura Mazda is answered by a plague from Angra Mainyu.

stories.canonicalTitle: Pele's journey to Halemaʻumaʻu
stories.titleZh: 佩蕾的旅程：从卡希基到哈雷茂茂
stories.summaryZh: 美国国家公园管理局概述夏威夷口述传统：火山女神佩蕾生在遥远的卡希基，为寻找适合她的火与家人的居所，远航来到夏威夷群岛，一路向东南迁移，最后在基拉韦厄山顶的哈雷茂茂火山口安家，据说至今仍住在那里。按照夏威夷传统，经过她的土地要先请求许可。
stories.summaryEn: The National Park Service summarizes Hawaiian oral history: the volcano deity Pele was born in distant Kahiki and voyaged to the Hawaiian Islands seeking a home for her fire and family, moving southeast until she settled in Halemaʻumaʻu crater at the summit of Kīlauea, where she is said still to live. In Hawaiian tradition one asks her permission to travel through her land.
stories.editorialNote: 须署名的公开概述：依据美国国家公园管理局两页公开介绍；各家族与地方的 moʻolelo 版本差异很大，本站不收集。

sections.bodyEn: The National Park Service explains that, in oral history, Pele is the Hawaiian volcano deity, an elemental force and the creator of these volcanic landscapes. Born in the distant land of Kahiki, she voyaged to the Hawaiian Islands to find a suitable home for her fire and family.

sections.headingEn: Island by island to the southeast
sections.bodyZh: 她一座岛一座岛地向东南迁移，寻找能安顿下来的地方。
sections.bodyEn: She moved southeast through the islands, one after another, looking for a place to settle.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 各岛上的具体经历因版本而异，本站不补写。

sections.bodyZh: 最后她来到基拉韦厄山顶的哈雷茂茂火山口，把这里定为永久的家。据说她至今仍住在那里。
sections.bodyEn: At last she came to Halemaʻumaʻu crater at the summit of Kīlauea and made it her permanent home. She is said to live there still.

sections.bodyZh: 在夏威夷传统中，经过佩蕾的土地要先请求她的许可。国家公园管理局也请访客在这片神圣的地景中保持尊重。公园还提醒：不同的 moʻolelo 版本可能差别很大。
sections.bodyEn: In Hawaiian tradition it is customary to ask Pele's permission to travel through her land, and the park asks visitors to behave respectfully in this sacred landscape. It also notes that versions of the moʻolelo may differ, sometimes greatly.

readingRoutes.evidencePolicy: Each step keeps its own witness; textual witnesses never determine a material witness's recension, and later retellings are not back-projected.

deityStoryCards.name: Fuxi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《系辞下》中的包牺氏（伏羲）：仰观天象、俯察地法，始作八卦，又结绳为网。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Baoxi (Fuxi) in Xi Ci II: the ancient ruler who observed heaven, earth and living things, first made the eight trigrams and knotted nets.

beats.textZh: 《系辞下》讲古代圣人的发明，第一位就是包牺氏——后世通常写作伏羲。书里说，远古的时候，是他在治理天下。
beats.textEn: Xi Ci II lists the inventions of the ancient sages, and the first is Baoxi — usually written Fuxi in later texts. In remote antiquity, it says, he ruled all under heaven.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)
beats.uncertaintyNote: “包牺”即“伏羲”是传统注疏的读法。

beats.textZh: 他抬头观察天上的日月星辰，低头观察大地的形势；又细看鸟兽身上的花纹，看各地适合生长什么。近处，他从自己的身体取法；远处，他从万物取法。
beats.textEn: He looked up at the images in the sky and down at the patterns of the earth; he studied the markings of birds and beasts and what each land was suited for. Near at hand he drew on his own body, and far off on all things.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)

beats.textZh: 于是他开始画出八卦——八个由三条线组成的符号，用来通达神明的德性，把万物的情状分门别类。
beats.textEn: Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams — eight figures of three lines each — to communicate with spirit-like virtue and to sort the dispositions of the myriad things.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)

beats.textZh: 他还把绳子打结，做成罗网，人们用它打猎、捕鱼。《系辞》接下来再讲神农等后来的圣人，这里只讲伏羲这一段。
beats.textEn: He also knotted cords into nets, which people used to hunt and fish. The Xi Ci then moves on to later sages such as Shennong; this retelling covers only Baoxi's part.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后续圣人的发明不在本故事范围内。

deityStoryCards.name: Gonggong
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Figure who contends with Zhuanxu and strikes Mount Buzhou in the Huainanzi Tian Wen and Liezi Tang Wen witnesses; whether deity, clan head or rival ruler is foregrounded varies by source and is not resolved here.

beats.textZh: 《淮南子·天文训》说，从前共工与颛顼争夺帝位。
beats.textEn: Huainanzi “Tian Wen” says that long ago Gonggong contended with Zhuanxu to become ruler.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Tian Wen Xun — passage opening 昔者共工
beats.uncertaintyNote: 颛顼在此作为传说中的君主登记，不作历史真实性判断。

beats.textZh: 共工发怒撞向不周山，支撑天的柱子折断，系住大地的绳索断绝。
beats.textEn: In anger Gonggong strikes Mount Buzhou; the pillar holding up heaven breaks and the cords binding the earth snap.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Tian Wen Xun — passage opening 昔者共工
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不周山不映射为现代山名或坐标。

beats.textZh: 结果天向西北倾斜，日月星辰随之移动；地在东南不满，积水与尘埃都归向那里。这一段没有提到女娲，是《天文训》中独立的天地形势解释。
beats.textEn: As a result heaven tilts to the northwest and the sun, moon and stars shift with it; the earth falls short in the southeast, where waters and dust collect. The passage does not mention Nüwa and stands as an independent explanation of cosmic orientation in “Tian Wen”.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Tian Wen Xun — passage opening 昔者共工
beats.uncertaintyNote: 同书《览冥训》的女娲段与此段分属不同章节，不合成单一故事。

facts.textZh: 共工出现在“共工触不周山”之中。
facts.textEn: Gonggong is the actor who strikes Mount Buzhou in both registered witnesses.

beats.textZh: 《淮南子·览冥训》以远古为背景：支撑天地的四极崩坏，九州开裂，天不能全覆、地不能全载，大火与洪水都无法止息，猛兽鸷鸟危害百姓。本段只按这一见证的顺序概述，不补入其他文献给出的起因。
beats.textEn: Huainanzi “Lan Ming” sets the scene in remote antiquity: the four poles holding up the world have failed and the nine provinces have split; heaven no longer covers everything and earth no longer bears everything, fires and floods cannot be stopped, and wild beasts and birds of prey attack the people. This section follows only this witness and adds no cause taken from other texts.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.uncertaintyNote: 传世本用字存在异体；本站只发布独立概述，不复制整段原文。

beats.headingEn: Five-colored stones and the turtle's legs
beats.textZh: 于是女娲炼五色石来修补苍天，又截断巨鳌的足，用来重新立起四极。
beats.textEn: Nüwa then refines five-colored stones to patch the azure sky and cuts off the legs of a great turtle to set the four poles upright again.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.uncertaintyNote: 炼字与鳌字在不同版本中有异体，不影响本段概述。

beats.headingEn: The black dragon and the reed ash
beats.textZh: 这一见证还写到女娲杀死黑龙以救济冀州，并堆积芦苇灰来堵住泛滥的洪水；随后天地重新安定，百姓得以存活。
beats.textEn: This witness adds that Nüwa kills a black dragon to relieve Jizhou and piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters; afterwards heaven and earth are set right and the people survive.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.uncertaintyNote: 冀州在此是文本中的九州之一，不映射为现代行政区或坐标；《列子·汤问》对应段落未陈述这两项。

beats.textZh: 《览冥训》的女娲段落没有把天地崩坏归因于共工。《淮南子》确实在《天文训》另记共工怒触不周山，但那是另一章中独立的天地倾斜起源，本站不把两章拼接成因果链。
beats.textEn: The Lan Ming Nüwa passage does not attribute the collapse to Gonggong. The Huainanzi does narrate Gonggong striking Mount Buzhou, but in a separate passage in the “Tian Wen” chapter that explains the tilt of heaven and earth; the site does not splice the two chapters into a causal chain.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.uncertaintyNote: 把共工触山写成女娲补天起因的说法见于较晚文献，已作为独立接受层排队。

facts.textZh: 女娲出现在“女娲补天”之中。
facts.textEn: Nüwa is the actor who repairs the sky in both registered witnesses.
facts.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — Nüwa repair sentence group

facts.textZh: 女娲——情节：Piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters.
facts.textEn: In the Huainanzi Lan Ming witness Nüwa piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters.
facts.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — reed ash and flood waters

deityStoryCards.name: Pangu
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 徐整《三五历纪》佚文中的盘古：生于如鸡子的混沌之中，天地分开时日长一丈。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Pangu as quoted from Xu Zheng's lost Sanwu liji: born in an egg-like chaos, he grows a zhang a day as heaven and earth separate.

beats.textZh: 很久以前，天和地还没有分开，到处是一团混沌，样子像一个鸡蛋。盘古就生在这团混沌之中。
beats.textEn: Long ago heaven and earth were not yet apart; everything was one chaos shaped like a hen's egg, and Pangu was born inside it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 原书已佚，只能依靠类书引文。

beats.textZh: 过了一万八千年，天地开辟：轻而清的阳气上升成为天，重而浊的阴气下沉成为地。盘古就在天地之间，一天之中变化九次，比天更神，比地更圣。
beats.textEn: After 18,000 years heaven and earth opened: the light, clear yang rose to become heaven, the heavy, murky yin sank to become earth. Pangu stood between them, changing nine times a day, more divine than heaven and wiser than earth.

beats.textZh: 从此天每天升高一丈，地每天加厚一丈，盘古也每天长高一丈。这样又过了一万八千年，天高到了极点，地深到了极点，盘古也长到了极点。在这之后，才有了三皇。
beats.textEn: From then on heaven rose a zhang each day, earth grew a zhang thicker, and Pangu grew a zhang taller. After another 18,000 years heaven was as high as it could be, earth as deep, and Pangu as tall. Only after that came the Three Sovereigns.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “盘古垂死化身为日月山川”出自另一部书，本故事不合并。

deityStoryCards.name: Thunder Spirit of Leize
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《山海经·海内东经》的雷泽无名雷神；与后世雷公不自动合并。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Unnamed thunder spirit of Leize in the Classic of Mountains and Seas; not automatically merged with later Leigong.

beats.textZh: 《山海经·海内东经》的登记段落在雷泽描写一位无名雷神。
beats.textEn: The registered Hai Nei Dong Jing passage describes an unnamed thunder spirit in Leize.
beats.sourceTitle: Classic of Mountains and Seas, Hai Nei Dong Jing
beats.uncertaintyNote: “雷泽雷神”是数据库定位名，不是文本给出的专名。

beats.textZh: 该段把雷声与神灵击打腹部相连，系统把它保存为文本中的神话叙述。
beats.textEn: The passage connects thunder with the spirit striking its belly, and the system preserves this as a mythic statement in the text.
beats.sourceTitle: Classic of Mountains and Seas, Hai Nei Dong Jing
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把神话陈述当作自然科学解释。

beats.textZh: 因为文本没有给出后世雷公的专名与完整形象，系统不按“雷神”这个共通标签自动合并。
beats.textEn: Because the passage does not give the later proper name and full image of Leigong, the system does not merge the figures under the generic label thunder god.
beats.sourceTitle: Classic of Mountains and Seas, Hai Nei Dong Jing
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后世接受史将在独立版本中处理。

deityStoryCards.name: Yellow Emperor
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《史记·五帝本纪》中少典之子轩辕，于涿鹿擒杀蚩尤并被尊为天子；本站不作历史真实性断言。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Xuanyuan, son of Shaodian, who in the Shiji fights Chiyou at Zhuolu and is honoured as Son of Heaven; no historical-reality claim is made.

beats.textZh: 黄帝是少典的儿子，姓公孙，名轩辕。他那个时代，神农氏的统治衰落了，诸侯互相攻打、欺压百姓，神农氏却无力征讨。轩辕于是操练军队，去讨伐不肯朝贡的诸侯。
beats.textEn: The Yellow Emperor was the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan. In his time the rule of Shennong had declined; the lords attacked one another and oppressed the people, and Shennong could not punish them. So Xuanyuan trained troops to subdue the lords who would not pay tribute.
beats.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前轩辕与炎帝在阪泉的三次交战本故事未展开。

beats.textZh: 诸侯之中，蚩尤最为凶暴，没有人能制服他。蚩尤起来作乱，不听从帝王的命令。
beats.textEn: Among the lords Chiyou was the most violent, and no one could subdue him. Chiyou rose in rebellion and would not obey the ruler's command.
beats.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors

beats.textZh: 轩辕征召各路诸侯的军队，在涿鹿的原野上与蚩尤交战，终于把蚩尤擒住并杀死。
beats.textEn: Xuanyuan called up the armies of the lords and fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, and at last captured and killed him.
beats.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
beats.uncertaintyNote: 涿鹿不在本站映射为现代坐标。

beats.textZh: 诸侯们都尊奉轩辕为天子，取代了神农氏，这就是黄帝。
beats.textEn: The lords all honoured Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong: this was the Yellow Emperor.
beats.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors

facts.textZh: 黄帝出现在“涿鹿之战”之中。
facts.textEn: The Yellow Emperor levies the lords' troops and fights Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu.
facts.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
facts.sourceLocation: Wu di ben ji (與蚩尤戰於涿鹿之野)

facts.textZh: 黄帝——情节：trains troops while Shennong's rule declines
facts.textEn: As the house of Shennong declines and the lords attack one another, Xuanyuan trains troops to punish those who do not bring tribute.
facts.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
facts.sourceLocation: Wu di ben ji, Shennong decline passage

deityStoryCards.name: Nezha
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《西游记》第四回中托塔李天王的三太子，变三头六臂迎战孙悟空（后世文学层）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Third prince of Heavenly King Li in Journey to the West ch. 4, who takes three heads and six arms against Sun Wukong (later literary layer).

beats.textZh: 孙悟空发现“弼马温”只是个看马的小官，一气之下回到花果山，自称“齐天大圣”。玉帝派托塔李天王和他的三太子哪吒，带领天兵前去捉拿。
beats.textEn: Discovering that his title merely made him a keeper of horses, Sun Wukong storms back to his mountain and calls himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven. The Jade Emperor sends Heavenly King Li, bearer of the pagoda, and his third son Nezha with the heavenly troops to seize him.

beats.textZh: 哪吒大喝一声，变成三头六臂，六只手各拿一件兵器打来。悟空见了，也变成三头六臂，把金箍棒一晃变成三条，六只手拿着架住。
beats.textEn: Nezha gives a shout and becomes a figure with three heads and six arms, a weapon in every hand. Wukong does the same: he shakes his staff into three and parries with six hands.

beats.textZh: 两人斗得难分难解。悟空拔下一根毫毛，变成自己的模样继续迎敌，真身却绕到哪吒背后打了一棒。哪吒负痛败走，回去禀报父王：这猴子神通广大。
beats.textEn: Neither can win. Wukong plucks a hair and turns it into a double of himself to keep fighting, while his true body circles behind Nezha and strikes. Nezha flees in pain and reports to his father that the monkey's powers are great.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是小说情节，属于后世文学层。

facts.textZh: 哪吒出现在“哪吒大战孙悟空（《西游记》第四回）”之中。
facts.textEn: Nezha is sent with Heavenly King Li to capture the self-styled Great Sage.

deityStoryCards.name: Leigong
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 跨时期雷神人格入口；先秦诗歌、汉代批判记录、敦煌图像与后世信仰分层登记。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Diachronic thunder-deity entry with classical poetic, Han critical, Dunhuang visual and later layers kept separate.

beats.textZh: 莫高窟第249窟中有雷公的形象。
beats.textEn: Dunhuang Academy identifies a thunder-deity image in Cave 249.
beats.sourceTitle: 敦煌岁时节令｜惊蛰：“爆裂鼓手”醒万物

beats.textZh: 莫高窟第285窟中有雷公的形象。
beats.textEn: Dunhuang Academy identifies a Western Wei thunder-deity image with twelve linked drums in Cave 285.
beats.sourceTitle: 敦煌岁时节令｜惊蛰：“爆裂鼓手”醒万物

beats.textZh: 论衡 · describes · 雷公
beats.textEn: The Lei Xu discussion describes a strong figure striking linked drums.

beats.textZh: 雷公出现在楚辞中。
beats.textEn: Chu Ci, Yuan You places Leigong to the right as a guard while the Rain Master attends on the left.

beats.textZh: 雷公出现在论衡中。
beats.textEn: Lunheng, Lei Xu records an image called Leigong with linked drums and a mallet, then criticizes that explanation as false.

beats.textZh: 雷公与莫高窟第285窟相关。
beats.textEn: The Dunhuang Academy identifies thunder-deity imagery in the real Western Wei Cave 285 ceiling program.

facts.textZh: 雷公与雷相关。
facts.textEn: Yuan You and Lei Xu provide early textual layers for a figure called Leigong in thunder-related imagery and escort language.
facts.sourceLocation: Chu Ci Yuan You; Lunheng Lei Xu

beats.textZh: 乌加里特伊勒——角色：creator; head of the pantheon
beats.textEn: The same overview names El as the creator at the head of the pantheon.

beats.textZh: 乌加里特巴力是乌加里特伊勒的孩子。
beats.textEn: Other relational language places Baal under El’s paternity in the Ugaritic divine-family discourse.
beats.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance

beats.textZh: 阿西拉特／亚舍拉与乌加里特伊勒是配偶。
beats.textEn: Penn Museum describes a Canaanite pantheon of El the creator and his consort Athirat (Asherah), with the storm god Baal and his sister Anat.

deityStoryCards.name: Baal of Ugarit
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 乌加里特 Baʿlu／Haddu：风暴、降雨、战士、土地与王权层按 KTU 泥板和图像证据登记。“Baal”亦为头衔，绝不自动合并所有同名神。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Ugaritic Baʿlu/Haddu in tablet and iconographic witnesses; Baal is also a title, so other Baal-named figures remain separate.

beats.textZh: KTU 1.2 IV把巴力与雅姆置于同一战斗事件中；库存记录确保故事锚定到具体泥板。
beats.textEn: KTU 1.2 IV places Baal and Yamm in the same combat event; the inventory record anchors the story to a specific tablet.
beats.sourceTitle: Ras Shamra tablet inventory record for KTU 1.2
beats.uncertaintyNote: 库存页本身不是完整译文。

beats.textZh: 已登记的学术资料把Yagrush与Ayyamur列为巴力依次使用的有名武器。
beats.textEn: Registered scholarship identifies Yagrush and Ayyamur as named weapons used in sequence by Baal.
beats.sourceTitle: Ras Shamra tablet inventory record for KTU 1.2
beats.uncertaintyNote: 武器中文名采用音译，不推定功能相同。

beats.textZh: 事件档案记录第二件武器使雅姆倒地；后续层仍受泥板状态与当前校勘范围限制。
beats.textEn: The event profile records the second weapon bringing Yamm down; what follows remains limited by tablet condition and current editorial coverage.
beats.sourceTitle: Ras Shamra tablet inventory record for KTU 1.2
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把残缺处补成连续对白。

facts.textZh: 乌加里特巴力 · bears title · 乌加里特 bʿl“主／领主”头衔
facts.textEn: The Ugaritic storm deity is associated with the bʿl title/name while remaining distinct from the lexeme node.
facts.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance

facts.textZh: 乌加里特巴力是乌加里特文本中的达贡／达甘的孩子。
facts.textEn: Ugaritic textual formulae call Baal son of Dagan.
facts.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance

facts.textZh: 乌加里特巴力是乌加里特伊勒的孩子。

facts.textZh: 乌加里特巴力与雅姆为敌。
facts.textEn: The Ugaritic Baal Cycle presents a conflict involving Baal and Yam.
facts.sourceLocation: KTU 1.1 fragment and wider Baal Cycle context

facts.textZh: 乌加里特巴力与闪电相关。
facts.textEn: The Louvre stele depicts Baal with thunder/lightning iconography.

facts.textZh: 乌加里特巴力出现在“巴力与穆特事件序列（KTU 1.5–1.6）”之中。
facts.textEn: Baal participates in the KTU 1.5–1.6 sequence.
facts.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance

deityStoryCards.nameZh: 乌加里特文本中的达贡／达甘
deityStoryCards.name: Dagan in Ugaritic texts
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 只按乌加里特文本中的神名与巴力亲属称谓建档，不与其他时期地方达贡传统粗暴合并。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Witness-scoped Ugaritic Dagan dossier.

beats.textZh: 乌加里特巴力是乌加里特文本中的达贡／达甘的孩子。

beats.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance

deityStoryCards.hookZh: KTU 1.2 IV 中为巴力制作两件有名武器的工艺神。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Craft deity who makes two named weapons for Baal in KTU 1.2 IV.

facts.textEn: KTU 1.2 IV identifies Kothar-wa-Khasis as maker of Ayyamur for Baal.
facts.sourceTitle: Baal weapons Yagrush and Ayyamur in KTU 1.2 IV

facts.textZh: 科塔尔-瓦-哈西斯创造了亚格鲁什。
facts.textEn: KTU 1.2 IV identifies Kothar-wa-Khasis as maker of Yagrush for Baal.
facts.sourceTitle: Baal weapons Yagrush and Ayyamur in KTU 1.2 IV

beats.textZh: KTU 1.5–1.6的语料登记把巴力与穆特放在同一残缺事件序列。
beats.textEn: The KTU 1.5–1.6 corpus record places Baal and Mot in one fragmentary event sequence.
beats.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不同泥板栏位尚未逐栏发布到本站。

beats.textZh: 阿纳特也被已验证的参与Claim连接到巴力—穆特的恢复序列。
beats.textEn: A verified participant claim also links Anat to the Baal-Mot recovery sequence.
beats.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance
beats.uncertaintyNote: 具体动作等待逐栏校勘。

beats.headingEn: Return is not the end of death
beats.textZh: 巴力在叙事序列中返回，但系统明确不把它解释为“死亡永久被消灭”的普遍命题。
beats.textEn: Baal returns within the narrative sequence, but the system explicitly does not interpret this as a universal claim that death was permanently destroyed.
beats.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance
beats.uncertaintyNote: 避免把残缺神话普遍化。

facts.textZh: 穆特出现在“巴力与穆特事件序列（KTU 1.5–1.6）”之中。

facts.sourceTitle: Baˁlu Epic KTU 1.1–1.6 — corpus and tablet concordance

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Athirat (Asherah), consort of El the creator in the Penn Museum's overview of the Canaanite pantheon.

beats.textZh: 阿西拉特／亚舍拉与乌加里特伊勒是配偶。
beats.textEn: Penn Museum describes a Canaanite pantheon of El the creator and his consort Athirat (Asherah), with the storm god Baal and his sister Anat.
