facts.sourceLocation: KTU 1.1 fragment and wider Baal Cycle context

facts.textZh: 雅姆出现在“巴力与雅姆之战（KTU 1.2 IV）”之中。
facts.textEn: Yamm is Baal’s opponent in the KTU 1.2 IV event layer.
facts.sourceTitle: Ras Shamra tablet inventory record for KTU 1.2

deityStoryCards.name: Ashur
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 与亚述城相关的神；联合国教科文组织称该城为亚述人的宗教首都。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: God associated with the city of Ashur, which UNESCO calls the religious capital of the Assyrians.

beats.textZh: 阿舒尔在阿舒尔受到崇拜。
beats.textEn: UNESCO describes the city of Ashur as the religious capital of the Assyrians, associated with the god Ashur.

deityStoryCards.name: Ullr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 希芙之子；《诗语法》据此称索尔为其继父。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Sif; Skaldskaparmal consequently calls Thor his stepfather.

beats.textZh: 希芙是乌勒尔的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Ullr as Sif’s son.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是乌勒尔的继父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal calls Thor the stepfather of Ullr.

deityStoryCards.name: Borr
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Búri and father of Odin, Vili and Vé in Gylfaginning.

beats.textZh: 博尔是布里的孩子。
beats.textEn: Gylfaginning presents Borr as Búri’s son.

beats.textZh: 博尔是奥丁的父母。
beats.textEn: Borr is father of Odin in Gylfaginning.

beats.textZh: 博尔是维的父母。
beats.textEn: Borr is father of Vé in Gylfaginning.

beats.textZh: 博尔是维利的父母。
beats.textEn: Borr is father of Vili in Gylfaginning.

beats.textZh: 博尔与贝斯特拉是配偶。
beats.textEn: Gylfaginning presents Borr and Bestla as parents together.

beats.textZh: 当前数据库把诸神黄昏登记为世界终末与更新类型的神话事件。
beats.textEn: The current database registers Ragnarok as a mythic event of world ending and renewal.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 完整事件阶段仍未全部结构化。

beats.textZh: 已验证的参与Claims把奥丁与芬里尔放入这场战斗。
beats.textEn: Verified participant claims place Odin and Fenrir in this battle.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 其他参与者将在逐见证扩张后加入。

beats.textZh: 毁灭、存活与更新的完整次序仍是研究缺口；网页不会借电影或游戏情节把它补成“完整故事”。
beats.textEn: The full order of destruction, survival, and renewal remains a research gap; films and games are not used to fill it into a supposedly complete story.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 明确标记为PARTIAL。

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是奥丁的孩子。
facts.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Thor as a son of Odin.

facts.textZh: 贝斯特拉是奥丁的父母。
facts.textEn: Bestla is mother of Odin in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 博尔是奥丁的父母。
facts.textEn: Borr is father of Odin in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 维与奥丁是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Vé and Odin are brothers in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 维利与奥丁是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Vili and Odin are brothers in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 弗丽嘉与奥丁是配偶。
facts.textEn: Frigg is Odin's wife and knows all fates, though she does not prophesy.

deityStoryCards.name: Ymir
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 在金伦加鸿沟中形成的原初巨人；被奥丁兄弟杀死，世界由他的身体造成（《欺骗古鲁菲》第5–8章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Primordial giant formed in Ginnungagap; killed by Odin and his brothers, who make the world from his body (Gylfaginning 5–8).

beats.textZh: 世界还不存在时，只有一道叫金伦加的深渊。北方的寒霜与南方的热气在这里相遇，融化的水滴里生出了巨人尤弥尔。
beats.textEn: Before the world exists there is only the void of Ginnungagap. Where rime from the north meets heat from the south, the thawing drops bring forth the giant Ymir.

beats.headingEn: Odin and his brothers kill Ymir
beats.textZh: 布尔的儿子们——奥丁、维利和维——杀死了巨人尤弥尔。
beats.textEn: The sons of Borr — Odin, Vili and Vé — kill the giant Ymir.

beats.headingEn: A world made from a body
beats.textZh: 他们用尤弥尔的身体造出世界：肉变成大地，血变成海洋和湖泊，骨头变成山岩，头骨被举起来成为天空。
beats.textEn: From Ymir's body they make the world: his flesh becomes the earth, his blood the sea and lakes, his bones the rocks, and his skull is raised up as the sky.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里的散文综述与诗歌见证可能有细节差异。

facts.textZh: 尤弥尔出现在“尤弥尔被杀与世界成形”之中。
facts.textEn: Ymir's body becomes the material of the world.

deityStoryCards.name: Njörðr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第23章中的华纳神：住在诺欧通，掌管风与海，是弗雷与芙蕾雅之父。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Vanir god in Gylfaginning 23: lives at Nóatún, rules wind and sea, father of Freyr and Freyja.

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德住在天上一个叫诺欧通的地方。他掌管风的运行，能平息海浪和火焰；出海航行和捕鱼的人都向他祈祷。他在华纳海姆长大，后来作为人质被送到阿萨神族。
beats.textEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún. He rules the motion of the wind and can calm sea and fire; those who sail or fish pray to him. He was raised in Vanaheim and later given to the Æsir as a hostage.

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德有一儿一女。儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和大地的收成，人们向他祈求丰年与富足。女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每当她骑马出战，就分得一半战死者，另一半归奥丁；她乘坐的车由两只猫拉着。
beats.textEn: Njörðr has a son and a daughter. Freyr rules rain, sunshine and the produce of the earth, and people pray to him for good seasons and wealth. Freyja lives at Fólkvangr; whenever she rides to battle she takes half the slain, Odin the other half, and her chariot is drawn by two cats.

beats.textZh: 后来，弗雷爱上了巨人之女葛德。为了娶到她，他把自己的宝剑交给了别人作为代价——这把剑从此不在他手中。
beats.textEn: Later Freyr falls in love with Gerðr, a giant's daughter. To win her he gives away his sword as the price, and the sword is no longer his.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 葛德尚未单独建立实体；诸神黄昏中的后果另行登记。

facts.textZh: 芙蕾雅是尼奥尔德的孩子。
facts.textEn: Njörðr's daughter is Freyja.

facts.textZh: 弗雷是尼奥尔德的孩子。
facts.textEn: Njörðr's son is Freyr.

facts.textZh: 尼奥尔德居于诺欧通。
facts.textEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at the place called Nóatún.

facts.textZh: 尼奥尔德——来历：raised in Vanaheim; hostage to the Æsir
facts.textEn: Njörðr was brought up in Vanaheim and given to the Æsir as a hostage.

beats.headingEn: The goddess who knows all fates
beats.textZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子。斯诺里说，她知道一切人的命运，只是从不说出来。
beats.textEn: Frigg is Odin's wife. Snorri says she knows the fates of all, though she does not speak them aloud.

beats.textZh: 巴德尔做了不祥的梦。弗丽嘉便去找火、水、铁和各种金属、石头、土地、树木、疾病、野兽、鸟和蛇，让它们都发誓不伤害巴德尔。只有长在英灵殿西边的一株小槲寄生，她觉得太小，没有让它发誓。
beats.textEn: Baldr has ominous dreams, so Frigg makes fire, water, iron and all metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds and serpents swear not to harm him. Only a young mistletoe shoot she thinks too small to ask.

beats.textZh: 众神以为巴德尔刀枪不入，便拿东西扔他取乐。然而那株没有发誓的槲寄生被做成了投枪，巴德尔被它刺中而死。
beats.textEn: Believing Baldr unharmable, the gods amuse themselves by throwing things at him. But the mistletoe that never swore is made into a dart, and Baldr is struck down and dies.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 投掷者与幕后之人的情节将在后续批次逐段登记。

facts.textZh: 巴德尔是弗丽嘉的孩子。
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning presents Frigg as Baldr's mother in the account of his death.

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔与巴德尔是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Haustlong stanza 16 uses brother terminology for Thor and Baldr.

deityStoryCards.name: Búri
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Ancestor licked free from rime by Auðhumla in Gylfaginning.

beats.textZh: 博尔是布里的孩子。
beats.textEn: Gylfaginning presents Borr as Búri’s son.

deityStoryCards.name: Sif
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《诗语法》所见索尔之妻、乌勒尔之母与斯露德母系见证。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Wife of Thor, mother of Ullr and mother of Thrud in registered medieval witnesses.

beats.textZh: 希芙是斯露德的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal identifies Thrud through Sif in its kinship terminology.

beats.textZh: 希芙是乌勒尔的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Ullr as Sif’s son.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔与希芙是配偶。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal calls Thor the husband of Sif.

deityStoryCards.name: Frigg
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 奥丁之妻，知晓一切命运；她让万物发誓不伤害巴德尔，唯独漏掉了槲寄生（《欺骗古鲁菲》第20、49章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Odin's wife who knows all fates; she takes oaths from all things to protect Baldr, except the mistletoe (Gylfaginning 20, 49).

beats.headingEn: The goddess who knows all fates
beats.textZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子。斯诺里说，她知道一切人的命运，只是从不说出来。
beats.textEn: Frigg is Odin's wife. Snorri says she knows the fates of all, though she does not speak them aloud.

beats.uncertaintyNote: 投掷者与幕后之人的情节将在后续批次逐段登记。

facts.textZh: 巴德尔是弗丽嘉的孩子。
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning presents Frigg as Baldr's mother in the account of his death.

deityStoryCards.name: Freyr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 尼奥尔德之子，掌管雨水、阳光与丰收；为娶葛德而交出宝剑（《欺骗古鲁菲》第24、37章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Njörðr who rules rain, sunshine and the fruitfulness of the earth; gives away his sword to win Gerðr (Gylfaginning 24, 37).

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德住在天上一个叫诺欧通的地方。他掌管风的运行，能平息海浪和火焰；出海航行和捕鱼的人都向他祈祷。他在华纳海姆长大，后来作为人质被送到阿萨神族。
beats.textEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún. He rules the motion of the wind and can calm sea and fire; those who sail or fish pray to him. He was raised in Vanaheim and later given to the Æsir as a hostage.

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德有一儿一女。儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和大地的收成，人们向他祈求丰年与富足。女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每当她骑马出战，就分得一半战死者，另一半归奥丁；她乘坐的车由两只猫拉着。
beats.textEn: Njörðr has a son and a daughter. Freyr rules rain, sunshine and the produce of the earth, and people pray to him for good seasons and wealth. Freyja lives at Fólkvangr; whenever she rides to battle she takes half the slain, Odin the other half, and her chariot is drawn by two cats.

beats.textZh: 后来，弗雷爱上了巨人之女葛德。为了娶到她，他把自己的宝剑交给了别人作为代价——这把剑从此不在他手中。
beats.textEn: Later Freyr falls in love with Gerðr, a giant's daughter. To win her he gives away his sword as the price, and the sword is no longer his.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 葛德尚未单独建立实体；诸神黄昏中的后果另行登记。

facts.textZh: 弗雷——职掌：rain, sunshine and the fruitfulness of the earth
facts.textEn: Freyr rules rain and sunshine and the produce of the earth, and is invoked for prosperity.

facts.textZh: 弗雷是尼奥尔德的孩子。
facts.textEn: Njörðr's son is Freyr.

facts.textZh: 弗雷与芙蕾雅是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Freyr and Freyja are the children of Njörðr.

deityStoryCards.name: Týr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 众神中最勇敢的一位；束缚芬里尔时失去一只手（《欺骗古鲁菲》第25、34章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: The boldest of the gods, who loses his hand when the wolf Fenrir is bound (Gylfaginning 25, 34).

beats.textZh: 斯诺里说，提尔是众神中最勇敢、最无畏的一位，打仗时人们向他祈求胜利。他只有一只手。
beats.textEn: Snorri says Týr is the boldest and most valiant of the gods, invoked for victory in battle — and he has only one hand.

beats.textZh: 众神想用一条魔法绳索捆住狼芬里尔。狼起了疑心，要求有人把手放进它嘴里，保证这不是诡计。众神面面相觑，只有提尔伸出了右手。
beats.textEn: The gods mean to bind the wolf Fenrir with a magic fetter. Suspicious, the wolf demands that someone put a hand in its mouth as a pledge of good faith. Only Týr holds out his right hand.

beats.textZh: 绳索越挣越紧，狼发现自己被骗了，便咬断了提尔的手。众神都笑了，只有提尔没有笑。
beats.textEn: The more the wolf struggles, the tighter the fetter grows. Realizing it has been tricked, Fenrir bites off Týr's hand — and all the gods laugh, except Týr.

deityStoryCards.name: Thrud
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔与希芙之女；不是索尔的姐姐。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Thor and Sif, not Thor’s sister.

beats.textZh: 希芙是斯露德的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal identifies Thrud through Sif in its kinship terminology.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是斯露德的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Thrud as a child of Thor.

deityStoryCards.name: Meili
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 古诺斯诗语与斯诺里材料称索尔为梅利之兄弟；资料仍极少。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Thor is called Meili’s brother in registered poetic and Snorrian witnesses; the dossier remains sparse.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔与梅利是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Old Norse poetic and Snorrian witness terminology calls Thor the brother of Meili.

beats.textZh: 诗语法提到梅利。
beats.textEn: Skáldskaparmál preserves Meili in Thor-kenning material.

deityStoryCards.name: Loki
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 古诺斯文本中的洛基；与索尔在多则叙事中互动，但兄弟关系只登记在现代改编层。古诺斯赫尔为洛基与安格尔波达之女。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Loki in Old Norse witnesses, interacting with Thor without an ancient sibling claim; Hel is Loki and Angrboda’s daughter in Snorri’s witness.

beats.textZh: 《索列姆之歌》把索尔置于寻找妙尔尼尔的中心位置。
beats.textEn: Thrymskvida places Thor at the center of the search for Mjolnir.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前版不扩写尚未逐节入库的情节。

beats.textZh: 洛基在诗中同行并提供建议；这项同伴关系不表示索尔与洛基是兄弟。
beats.textEn: Loki accompanies and advises him in the poem; this companionship does not make Thor and Loki brothers.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 保持亲属关系与故事同伴关系分离。

beats.textZh: 当前证据层确认两者共同处于妙尔尼尔寻回故事，但婚礼伪装与逐节行动尚未在本版本拆成独立Claims。
beats.textEn: The current evidence layer confirms both figures in the recovery story, while the wedding disguise and stanza-by-stanza actions have not yet been modeled as separate claims.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 详情将在后续逐节版本扩充。

facts.textZh: 洛基是赫尔的父母。
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning names Hel as a child of Loki and Angrboda.
facts.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning

deityStoryCards.name: Lóðurr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《女巫的预言》人类起源三神见证中的独立神祇；与 Loki 或 Vé 的同一说仅作待审研究问题。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Distinct deity in Völuspá; proposed identities with Loki or Vé remain unasserted research questions.

beats.textZh: 《女巫预言》17–18节在最初人类段落中分别命名阿斯克与恩布拉。
beats.textEn: Voluspa 17–18 names Ask and Embla in its first-human episode.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前中文概述不复制现代译文。

beats.textZh: 这段诗歌把奥丁、赫尼尔与洛杜尔放在同一创造人类场景中。
beats.textEn: The poetic passage places Odin, Hoenir, and Lodurr together in the human-creation scene.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 各神具体赐予项目将在逐词校勘后补充。

beats.textZh: 这里记录的是诗歌三神组合；《欺骗古鲁菲》的奥丁、维利、维组合不会覆盖它。
beats.textEn: This is the poetic triad; the Odin, Vili, and Ve grouping in Gylfaginning does not overwrite it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 差异保持为版本并存，而非人物自动等同。

facts.textZh: 《女巫的预言》第17–18节见证提到洛杜尔。
facts.textEn: The passage names Lóðurr.

deityStoryCards.name: Heimdallr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 住在彩虹桥边希敏约格的众神守望者，掌管加拉尔号角（《欺骗古鲁菲》第27章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Watchman of the gods at Himinbjörg by Bifröst, keeper of Gjallarhorn (Gylfaginning 27).

beats.textZh: 海姆达尔是众神的守望者。他住在彩虹桥边一个叫希敏约格的地方，在天的尽头守着桥，防止山巨人闯进来。
beats.textEn: Heimdallr is the watchman of the gods. He lives at Himinbjörg by Bifröst, at the edge of heaven, guarding the bridge against the mountain-giants.

beats.textZh: 他需要的睡眠比鸟还少，无论白天黑夜都能看见一百里远；他还能听见草在地上生长、羊毛在羊身上生长的声音。
beats.textEn: He needs less sleep than a bird and sees a hundred leagues by day or night; he can hear grass growing in the ground and wool growing on sheep.

beats.headingZh: 加拉尔号角与九位母亲
beats.textZh: 海姆达尔有一支号角，叫加拉尔号角，吹响时所有世界都能听见。斯诺里还说，他是九位母亲的儿子，而这九位母亲是姐妹。
beats.textEn: Heimdallr has a horn called Gjallarhorn, whose blast is heard in all worlds. Snorri also says he is the son of nine mothers, who were sisters.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 九位母亲的名字见其他诗篇，本版不列出。

facts.textZh: 海姆达尔居于希敏约格。
facts.textEn: Heimdallr lives at Himinbjörg by Bifröst.

facts.textZh: 海姆达尔——来历：son of nine mothers, who were sisters
facts.textEn: Heimdallr is called the son of nine mothers, who were sisters.

deityStoryCards.name: Thor
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔／Þórr：古诺斯文本中的锤持有者、巨人对手与家谱节点；本版补齐父母、配偶、子女、梅利与洛基文本关系。洛基并非古诺斯层兄弟。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Thor in registered Old Norse witnesses, now linked to source-specific parents, spouse, children, Meili and Loki episodes; Loki is not his Old Norse brother.

beats.textZh: 《索列姆之歌》把索尔置于寻找妙尔尼尔的中心位置。
beats.textEn: Thrymskvida places Thor at the center of the search for Mjolnir.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前版不扩写尚未逐节入库的情节。

beats.textEn: Loki accompanies and advises him in the poem; this companionship does not make Thor and Loki brothers.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 保持亲属关系与故事同伴关系分离。

beats.textZh: 当前证据层确认两者共同处于妙尔尼尔寻回故事，但婚礼伪装与逐节行动尚未在本版本拆成独立Claims。
beats.textEn: The current evidence layer confirms both figures in the recovery story, while the wedding disguise and stanza-by-stanza actions have not yet been modeled as separate claims.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 详情将在后续逐节版本扩充。

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是约尔德／大地女神的孩子。
facts.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Thor as a son of Jord.

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是奥丁的孩子。
facts.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Thor as a son of Odin.

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是马格尼的父母。
facts.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Magni as a child of Thor.

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是莫迪的父母。
facts.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Modi as a child of Thor.

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是斯露德的父母。
facts.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Thrud as a child of Thor.

facts.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔与巴德尔是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Haustlong stanza 16 uses brother terminology for Thor and Baldr.

deityStoryCards.name: Jord
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《散文埃达》所见索尔之母；大地人格层与具体文本见证分开保存。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Mother of Thor in the registered Prose Edda witness; earth-personification scope remains witness-specific.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是约尔德／大地女神的孩子。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Thor as a son of Jord.

deityStoryCards.name: Vé
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Brother of Odin and Vili; participates in cosmogonic acts in Gylfaginning.

beats.textZh: 《欺骗古鲁菲》8–9章同样命名阿斯克与恩布拉，构成散文版的人类起源见证。
beats.textEn: Gylfaginning 8–9 also names Ask and Embla, forming the prose witness to human origins.
beats.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把散文版当作诗歌版的简单翻译。

beats.textZh: 散文序列把奥丁、维利与维列为博尔之子，并放在这一创造框架中。
beats.textEn: The prose sequence identifies Odin, Vili, and Ve as sons of Borr and places them in this creation frame.
beats.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning
beats.uncertaintyNote: 人物组合与《女巫预言》不同。

beats.textZh: 系统不把维利／维与赫尼尔／洛杜尔按功能相似强制合并；当前只呈现两个文本明确给出的名字。
beats.textEn: The system does not force Vili and Ve to equal Hoenir and Lodurr by perceived functional similarity; it presents only the names explicit in each text.
beats.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning
beats.uncertaintyNote: 身份对应留作研究问题。

facts.textZh: 维——角色：joins Odin and Vili in cosmogonic actions
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning includes Vé with Odin and Vili in forming the world from Ymir.

facts.textZh: 贝斯特拉是维的父母。
facts.textEn: Bestla is mother of Vé in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 博尔是维的父母。
facts.textEn: Borr is father of Vé in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 维与奥丁是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Vé and Odin are brothers in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 维利与维是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Vili and Vé are brothers in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第8–9章见证提到维。
facts.textEn: The prose sequence names Vé among Borr’s sons.
facts.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning

deityStoryCards.name: Vili
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Brother of Odin and Vé; participates in cosmogonic acts in Gylfaginning.

beats.textZh: 《欺骗古鲁菲》8–9章同样命名阿斯克与恩布拉，构成散文版的人类起源见证。
beats.textEn: Gylfaginning 8–9 also names Ask and Embla, forming the prose witness to human origins.
beats.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把散文版当作诗歌版的简单翻译。

beats.textZh: 散文序列把奥丁、维利与维列为博尔之子，并放在这一创造框架中。
beats.textEn: The prose sequence identifies Odin, Vili, and Ve as sons of Borr and places them in this creation frame.
beats.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning
beats.uncertaintyNote: 人物组合与《女巫预言》不同。

beats.textZh: 系统不把维利／维与赫尼尔／洛杜尔按功能相似强制合并；当前只呈现两个文本明确给出的名字。
beats.textEn: The system does not force Vili and Ve to equal Hoenir and Lodurr by perceived functional similarity; it presents only the names explicit in each text.
beats.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning
beats.uncertaintyNote: 身份对应留作研究问题。

facts.textZh: 维利——角色：joins Odin and Vé in cosmogonic actions
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning includes Vili with Odin and Vé in forming the world from Ymir.

facts.textZh: 贝斯特拉是维利的父母。
facts.textEn: Bestla is mother of Vili in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 博尔是维利的父母。
facts.textEn: Borr is father of Vili in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 维利与奥丁是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Vili and Odin are brothers in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 维利与维是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Vili and Vé are brothers in Gylfaginning.

facts.textZh: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第8–9章见证提到维利。
facts.textEn: The prose sequence names Vili among Borr’s sons.
facts.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning

deityStoryCards.name: Freyja
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 尼奥尔德之女；住在弗尔克范格，分得一半战死者，乘两只猫拉的车（《欺骗古鲁菲》第24章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Njörðr; lives at Fólkvangr, takes half the slain and drives a chariot drawn by two cats (Gylfaginning 24).

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德住在天上一个叫诺欧通的地方。他掌管风的运行，能平息海浪和火焰；出海航行和捕鱼的人都向他祈祷。他在华纳海姆长大，后来作为人质被送到阿萨神族。
beats.textEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún. He rules the motion of the wind and can calm sea and fire; those who sail or fish pray to him. He was raised in Vanaheim and later given to the Æsir as a hostage.

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德有一儿一女。儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和大地的收成，人们向他祈求丰年与富足。女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每当她骑马出战，就分得一半战死者，另一半归奥丁；她乘坐的车由两只猫拉着。
beats.textEn: Njörðr has a son and a daughter. Freyr rules rain, sunshine and the produce of the earth, and people pray to him for good seasons and wealth. Freyja lives at Fólkvangr; whenever she rides to battle she takes half the slain, Odin the other half, and her chariot is drawn by two cats.

beats.textZh: 后来，弗雷爱上了巨人之女葛德。为了娶到她，他把自己的宝剑交给了别人作为代价——这把剑从此不在他手中。
beats.textEn: Later Freyr falls in love with Gerðr, a giant's daughter. To win her he gives away his sword as the price, and the sword is no longer his.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 葛德尚未单独建立实体；诸神黄昏中的后果另行登记。

facts.textZh: 芙蕾雅是尼奥尔德的孩子。
facts.textEn: Njörðr's daughter is Freyja.

facts.textZh: 弗雷与芙蕾雅是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Freyr and Freyja are the children of Njörðr.

facts.textZh: 芙蕾雅——使用：a chariot drawn by two cats
facts.textEn: Freyja drives a chariot drawn by two cats.

facts.textZh: 芙蕾雅居于弗尔克范格。
facts.textEn: Freyja's dwelling is Fólkvangr.

deityStoryCards.name: Modi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔之子；当前所用家谱见证没有明确登记其母亲。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Thor; the registered genealogy witness does not name his mother.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是莫迪的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Modi as a child of Thor.

beats.textZh: 洛基是赫尔的父母。
beats.textEn: Gylfaginning names Hel as a child of Loki and Angrboda.
beats.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning

deityStoryCards.name: Hœnir
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《女巫的预言》人类起源三神见证中的独立神祇；不与 Vili 自动等同。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: A distinct deity in the Völuspá human-origin triad; not automatically identified with Vili.

beats.textZh: 《女巫预言》17–18节在最初人类段落中分别命名阿斯克与恩布拉。
beats.textEn: Voluspa 17–18 names Ask and Embla in its first-human episode.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前中文概述不复制现代译文。

beats.textZh: 这段诗歌把奥丁、赫尼尔与洛杜尔放在同一创造人类场景中。
beats.textEn: The poetic passage places Odin, Hoenir, and Lodurr together in the human-creation scene.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 各神具体赐予项目将在逐词校勘后补充。

beats.textZh: 这里记录的是诗歌三神组合；《欺骗古鲁菲》的奥丁、维利、维组合不会覆盖它。
beats.textEn: This is the poetic triad; the Odin, Vili, and Ve grouping in Gylfaginning does not overwrite it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 差异保持为版本并存，而非人物自动等同。

facts.textZh: 《女巫的预言》第17–18节见证提到赫尼尔。
facts.textEn: The passage names Hœnir.

deityStoryCards.name: Magni
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔之子；《诗语法》另称其母为雅恩莎撒。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Thor; Skaldskaparmal also names Jarnsaxa as his mother.

beats.textZh: 雅恩莎撒是马格尼的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal identifies Jarnsaxa as Magni’s mother.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是马格尼的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Magni as a child of Thor.

deityStoryCards.name: Kūrma
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Tortoise form assumed by Viṣṇu to support Mount Mandara in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness; kept separate from the Mahābhārata tortoise king Akūpāra.

beats.headingZh: 诸神与阿修罗暂时结盟
beats.headingEn: A truce between gods and asuras
beats.textZh: 《薄伽梵往世书》第八篇第5–6章中，诸神按毗湿奴的建议与阿修罗暂时结盟，合力拔起曼陀罗山并运往大海，毗湿奴亲自出手相助。
beats.textEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5–8.6, on Viṣṇu's advice the gods make a temporary truce with the asuras; together they uproot Mount Mandara and carry it toward the ocean, with Viṣṇu himself stepping in to help.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 运山过程的细节只作概述，待逐颂校对。

beats.headingEn: Viṣṇu takes the form of a tortoise
beats.textZh: 以婆苏吉为绳开始搅拌后，曼陀罗山沉入水中；毗湿奴化作巨龟潜到山下，用背托起大山。
beats.textEn: Once the churning begins with Vāsuki as the rope, Mount Mandara sinks into the water; Viṣṇu assumes the form of a giant tortoise, dives beneath it and raises the mountain on his back.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 与精校本的龟王阿库帕拉构成显式见证差异，不做身份等同。

beats.textZh: 搅拌最先产生可怕的毒药，向各方蔓延；众生求助于湿婆，湿婆把毒药饮下。
beats.textEn: The churning first produces a terrible poison that spreads in every direction; beings turn to Śiva, who drinks it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后续图像传统与虔信解释未在本批次逐句建模。

beats.textZh: 其后又涌现多种宝物与存在，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
beats.textEn: A series of treasures and beings then emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不与精校本合并。

beats.textZh: 阿修罗抢走甘露后，毗湿奴化身为摩希尼迷惑他们，并把甘露分给诸神。罗睺假扮天神混入其中饮下甘露，被日月指认后，毗湿奴以神盘斩下其头。
beats.textEn: When the asuras snatch the amṛta, Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī, captivates them and distributes the amṛta to the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, slips in and drinks; when the Sun and Moon point him out, Viṣṇu severs his head with the discus.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 罗睺后来的天体身份不在本批次建模。

facts.textZh: 俱利摩（龟形化身）是毗湿奴的一种形态。
facts.textEn: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness presents the supporting tortoise as a form assumed by Viṣṇu.

deityStoryCards.name: Mohinī
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Enchanting female form of Viṣṇu who distributes the amṛta in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness; the Mahābhārata witness is linked only through its own description of a deluding female form.

facts.textZh: 摩希尼是毗湿奴的一种形态。
facts.textEn: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness presents Mohinī as a form assumed by Viṣṇu.

deityStoryCards.name: Brahma
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《薄伽梵往世书》8.5 中，梵天带领受困的众神去见毗湿奴，随后才有乳海搅拌。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5 Brahmā leads the distressed gods to Viṣṇu before the churning of the ocean.

beats.textZh: 梵天出现在“乳海搅拌（文本叙事）”之中。
beats.textEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5 the distressed gods go to Brahmā, who leads them to the Lord Ajita (Viṣṇu) and praises him; the churning follows in 8.6–8.9.

deityStoryCards.name: Dhanvantari
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Divine figure who emerges from the churned ocean carrying the amṛta in both registered textual witnesses.

beats.textZh: 精校本《初篇》1.15 中，诸神聚集在须弥山上商议如何得到甘露；那罗延（毗湿奴）建议诸神与阿修罗一起搅动大海。
beats.textEn: In the critical edition at Ādiparvan 1.15, the gods gather on Mount Meru to deliberate how to obtain the amṛta; Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) advises that gods and asuras churn the ocean together.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “那罗延”在此按既有毗湿奴实体连接，不扩展神学解释。

beats.headingZh: 曼陀罗山、婆苏吉与龟王
beats.headingEn: Mandara, Vāsuki and the tortoise king
beats.textZh: 巨蛇阿难陀拔起曼陀罗山作为搅棒，龙王婆苏吉充当搅绳；山的底部由龟王阿库帕拉承托。这一见证没有说龟王是毗湿奴的化身。
beats.textEn: The serpent Ananta uproots Mount Mandara to serve as the churning rod and the nāga Vāsuki serves as the rope; the tortoise king Akūpāra bears the base of the mountain. This witness does not say that the tortoise king is a form of Viṣṇu.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 阿难陀拔山一项为中等置信度，待逐颂校对；阿难陀尚未单独建实体。

beats.headingZh: 檀文陀利捧着甘露出现
beats.textZh: 搅拌中先后涌现多种存在与宝物，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
beats.textEn: As the churning goes on, a series of beings and treasures emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不从其他版本补齐。

beats.headingEn: The deluding female form and Rāhu
beats.textZh: 阿修罗夺走甘露后，那罗延化作迷惑人的女子形象，把甘露取回交给诸神。罗睺假扮天神偷饮甘露，被日月揭发后，那罗延以神盘斩下其头；随后天神与阿修罗爆发大战。
beats.textEn: After the Dānavas seize the amṛta, Nārāyaṇa takes on a deluding female form and recovers it for the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, drinks some of it; when the Sun and Moon expose him, Nārāyaṇa cuts off his head with the discus, and a great battle between gods and Dānavas follows.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 专名实体“摩希尼”只连接《薄伽梵往世书》见证；此处保留“迷惑的女身”描述。

beats.headingEn: Scope of the constituted critical text
beats.textZh: 在精校本 1.15–1.17 的正文里，没有湿婆吞下毒药的情节。这只说明本定位“未陈述”，不代表所有写本或地方传统都没有；校勘记录与附录尚待逐项核对。
beats.textEn: The constituted critical text at 1.15–1.17 does not include Śiva swallowing the poison. This records only that the locator does not state it; it does not mean that every manuscript or regional tradition lacks it, and the apparatus and appendices still have to be checked.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 写本校勘与附录已作为独立研究队列排队。

facts.textEn: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness presents the supporting tortoise as a form assumed by Viṣṇu.

facts.textZh: 毗湿奴——化形：a deluding female form that recovers the amṛta from the Dānavas
facts.textEn: In the Mahābhārata critical-edition witness Nārāyaṇa assumes a deluding female form and recovers the amṛta from the Dānavas.
facts.sourceLocation: Mahābhārata CE, Ādiparvan 1.16–1.17 — deluding female form

facts.textZh: 毗湿奴出现在“乳海搅拌（文本叙事）”之中。
facts.textEn: Viṣṇu (also called Nārāyaṇa in the epic witness) takes part in the churning narrative in both registered witnesses.

beats.headingEn: Viṣṇu takes the form of a tortoise
beats.textZh: 以婆苏吉为绳开始搅拌后，曼陀罗山沉入水中；毗湿奴化作巨龟潜到山下，用背托起大山。
beats.textEn: Once the churning begins with Vāsuki as the rope, Mount Mandara sinks into the water; Viṣṇu assumes the form of a giant tortoise, dives beneath it and raises the mountain on his back.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 与精校本的龟王阿库帕拉构成显式见证差异，不做身份等同。

beats.textZh: 搅拌最先产生可怕的毒药，向各方蔓延；众生求助于湿婆，湿婆把毒药饮下。
beats.textEn: The churning first produces a terrible poison that spreads in every direction; beings turn to Śiva, who drinks it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后续图像传统与虔信解释未在本批次逐句建模。

beats.textZh: 其后又涌现多种宝物与存在，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
beats.textEn: A series of treasures and beings then emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不与精校本合并。

beats.textZh: 阿修罗抢走甘露后，毗湿奴化身为摩希尼迷惑他们，并把甘露分给诸神。罗睺假扮天神混入其中饮下甘露，被日月指认后，毗湿奴以神盘斩下其头。
beats.textEn: When the asuras snatch the amṛta, Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī, captivates them and distributes the amṛta to the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, slips in and drinks; when the Sun and Moon point him out, Viṣṇu severs his head with the discus.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 罗睺后来的天体身份不在本批次建模。

deityStoryCards.name: Isis
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 在 UCL 对奥西里斯故事的概述中，伊西斯收集奥西里斯的肢体并怀上荷鲁斯；大都会博物馆的哀悼像把她与奈芙蒂斯配成一对。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: In the UCL summary of the Osiris cycle Isis gathers Osiris's limbs and conceives Horus; Met mourning figures pair her with Nephthys.

beats.textZh: 在埃及的创世观念里，主要的创造者是太阳神，他也被称为阿图姆。他最先生出一男一女：舒和泰芙努特。学者认为“舒”这个名字和“干燥”有关，“泰芙努特”则代表湿润。
beats.textEn: In Egyptian creation thought the principal creator is the sun-god, also called Atum. His first offshoots are a son and a daughter, Shu and Tefnet; scholars link Shu's name to dryness and read Tefnet as moisture.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “干燥／湿润”是现代学者的词源解释。

beats.textZh: 舒和泰芙努特又生下两个孩子：大地之神盖布和天空女神努特。干燥与湿润，变成了坚实的大地和古埃及人眼中充满水的天空。
beats.textEn: Shu and Tefnet in turn produce two children: Geb, god of the earth, and Nut, goddess of the sky — dryness and moisture crystallised into solid earth and a sky the Egyptians thought of as watery.

beats.headingEn: Shu holds earth and sky apart
beats.textZh: 盖布和努特被舒分开，天在上、地在下。零散的古代记载暗示，这种分离必须被强制维持，否则天地还会继续生出神来。
beats.textEn: Shu separates Geb and Nut, sky above and earth below. Scattered references suggest the separation had to be enforced, or earth and sky would keep producing divine offspring.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是学者对零散材料的归纳，不是单一文本的原话。

beats.headingZh: 塞特、奥西里斯与伊西斯
beats.textZh: 后来，奥西里斯“无序的兄弟”塞特出于嫉妒杀害了他，把遗体分开，并取代他成为世界之王。伊西斯找回奥西里斯的肢体，让遗体恢复到足以受孕，生下了荷鲁斯。
beats.textEn: Later Osiris's anarchic brother Seth, out of jealousy, murders him, dismembers him and takes his place as king of the world. Isis collects the limbs and revives the body enough to conceive a child, Horus.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 古代文献中这个故事有许多版本；本站不合成“标准版”。

facts.textZh: 荷鲁斯是伊西斯的孩子。

facts.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Osiris cycle summary

facts.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Osiris cycle summary

deityStoryCards.name: Hathor
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 在《天牛之书》中，拉的眼睛喝下红色啤酒后回归的慈爱、母性的形象。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: In the Tale of the Heavenly Cow, the loving, maternal character to which the raging Eye of Ra returns after drinking red beer.

beats.textZh: 一部新王国时期的宗教文献记载：人们起来反叛太阳神拉。拉决定惩罚他们，后来他也离开人间，退到天上。
beats.textEn: A New Kingdom religious composition records that people rebel against the sun-god Ra. He resolves to punish them, and in the end he withdraws to the sky.
beats.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Tale of the Heavenly Cow

beats.textZh: 拉把自己的眼睛从身体里派出去，成为一个独立的“女儿”。她化作塞赫麦特——意思是“强大的女神”——几乎把人类全部消灭。

beats.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Tale of the Heavenly Cow
beats.uncertaintyNote: “强大的女神”是 UCL 给出的释义。

beats.textZh: 众神用计：他们把一湖啤酒染成红色，看起来像人血。她喝下后醉得香甜，脾气也软化下来，重新变回慈爱、温柔的哈托尔。
beats.textEn: The gods play a trick: they colour a lake of beer red to look like human blood. She drinks, becomes sweetly drunk, and reverts to her loving, maternal character as Hathor.
beats.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Tale of the Heavenly Cow
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是故事中的性格转变；数据库不把两位女神合并为同一实体。

facts.textZh: 哈托尔出现在“天牛之书中的人类惩罚”之中。
facts.textEn: Hathor is the loving, maternal character to which the goddess returns at the end of the episode.
facts.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Tale of the Heavenly Cow

beats.textEn: In Egyptian representations the two mourning goddesses accompany the body of Osiris, one at each end. The museum suggests these figures were presumably placed at either end of the deceased's sarcophagus.

beats.textEn: Shu and Tefnet in turn produce two children: Geb, god of the earth, and Nut, goddess of the sky — dryness and moisture crystallised into solid earth and a sky the Egyptians thought of as watery.

beats.textZh: 在埃及的创世观念里，主要的创造者是太阳神，他也被称为阿图姆。他最先生出一男一女：舒和泰芙努特。学者认为“舒”这个名字和“干燥”有关，“泰芙努特”则代表湿润。
beats.textEn: In Egyptian creation thought the principal creator is the sun-god, also called Atum. His first offshoots are a son and a daughter, Shu and Tefnet; scholars link Shu's name to dryness and read Tefnet as moisture.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “干燥／湿润”是现代学者的词源解释。

beats.textZh: 舒和泰芙努特又生下两个孩子：大地之神盖布和天空女神努特。干燥与湿润，变成了坚实的大地和古埃及人眼中充满水的天空。
beats.textEn: Shu and Tefnet in turn produce two children: Geb, god of the earth, and Nut, goddess of the sky — dryness and moisture crystallised into solid earth and a sky the Egyptians thought of as watery.

beats.headingEn: Shu holds earth and sky apart
beats.textZh: 盖布和努特被舒分开，天在上、地在下。零散的古代记载暗示，这种分离必须被强制维持，否则天地还会继续生出神来。
beats.textEn: Shu separates Geb and Nut, sky above and earth below. Scattered references suggest the separation had to be enforced, or earth and sky would keep producing divine offspring.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是学者对零散材料的归纳，不是单一文本的原话。

beats.headingZh: 塞特、奥西里斯与伊西斯
beats.textZh: 后来，奥西里斯“无序的兄弟”塞特出于嫉妒杀害了他，把遗体分开，并取代他成为世界之王。伊西斯找回奥西里斯的肢体，让遗体恢复到足以受孕，生下了荷鲁斯。
beats.textEn: Later Osiris's anarchic brother Seth, out of jealousy, murders him, dismembers him and takes his place as king of the world. Isis collects the limbs and revives the body enough to conceive a child, Horus.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 古代文献中这个故事有许多版本；本站不合成“标准版”。

facts.textZh: 荷鲁斯是伊西斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: UCL names Horus as the child Isis conceives from the revived Osiris.
facts.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Osiris cycle summary

facts.textZh: 荷鲁斯是奥西里斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: UCL names Horus as the child of Osiris conceived after his revival.
facts.sourceLocation: Gods and goddesses: creation — the Osiris cycle summary

facts.textZh: 拉-哈拉赫提是包含荷鲁斯的复合神名。
facts.textEn: Ra-Horakhty incorporates Horus specifically in the horizon-protector scope described by the registered catalogue.
facts.sourceTitle: Stela with man offering to Re-Harakhty, unfinished

facts.textZh: 阿尼纸草第3框描绘了荷鲁斯。
facts.textEn: Frame 3 of the Papyrus of Ani depicts Horus leading Ani.

deityStoryCards.name: Anubis
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 胡狼头神；在大英博物馆《阿尼纸草》第3框的称量心脏场景中扶稳天平。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Jackal-headed god who steadies the balance in the weighing of Ani's heart (British Museum EA10470,3).

beats.textZh: 画面中央是一座天平。左边的秤盘里放着阿尼的心脏，右边是一根羽毛，代表真理与秩序女神玛阿特。
beats.textEn: At the centre stands a balance. In the left pan lies Ani's heart; in the right, a feather representing Maat, goddess of truth and order.
beats.sourceLocation: EA10470,3 — museum description of the Hall of Judgment

beats.textZh: 胡狼头的阿努比斯跪在天平旁，拉着右边秤盘的绳子，扶稳天平的铅锤。博物馆的说明称他是“在防腐之所的那一位”。
beats.textEn: Jackal-headed Anubis kneels by the balance, holding the cord of the right-hand pan and steadying its plumb bob. The museum describes him as 'he who is in the place of embalming'.
beats.sourceLocation: EA10470,3 — museum description of the Hall of Judgment

beats.textZh: 托特在画中出现两次：一只小狒狒坐在天平顶端；右边站着朱鹭头的“众神书吏”，手持调色板和芦苇笔，准备记下审问的结果。
beats.textEn: Thoth appears twice: as a small baboon sitting on top of the balance, and as the ibis-headed scribe of the gods standing to the right with palette and reed, ready to write down the result.
beats.sourceLocation: EA10470,3 — museum description of the Hall of Judgment
beats.uncertaintyNote: 称量的最终结果和吞噬心脏的怪兽不在这条博物馆描述里，本站不补写。

facts.textZh: 阿努比斯——称号：he who is in the place of embalming
facts.textEn: The museum record gives Anubis the description 'he who is in the place of embalming'.
facts.sourceLocation: EA10470,3 — museum description of the Hall of Judgment

facts.textZh: 阿尼纸草第3框描绘了阿努比斯。
facts.textEn: The frame shows Anubis as a jackal-headed kneeling figure who steadies the plumb bob of the balance.
facts.sourceLocation: EA10470,3 — museum description of the Hall of Judgment

facts.textZh: 太阳升起与落下形态与阿图姆相关。

facts.textZh: 阿图姆出现在《亡灵书》第17咒文中。

deityStoryCards.name: Atum-Horakhty

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Composite address in a Chapter 15 sun-hymn witness, stored separately from Atum-Ra.

beats.textZh: 阿图姆-哈拉赫提是包含阿图姆的复合神名。

beats.textZh: 太阳赞歌：Assmann 标准赞歌 C′见于阿图姆-哈拉赫提。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Composite Atum-Ra dossier currently anchored to the Egyptian context of the Darius statue at Susa.

beats.textZh: 阿图姆-拉是包含阿图姆的复合神名。
beats.textEn: Atum-Ra is registered as a composite expression involving Atum.
beats.sourceLocation: UEE Late Period Temples v2, page 16

beats.textZh: 阿图姆-拉是包含拉／瑞的复合神名。
beats.textEn: Atum-Ra is registered as a composite expression involving Ra.
beats.sourceLocation: UEE Late Period Temples v2, page 16

beats.textZh: 阿图姆-拉——关联：Heliopolis

beats.textZh: 大流士一世与阿图姆-拉相关。

beats.textZh: 阿蒙在卡纳克受到崇拜。

beats.textZh: 阿蒙属于底比斯三神组。
beats.textEn: Amun is the father member of the Theban triad in the registered scholarly synthesis.

beats.textZh: 阿蒙-拉是包含阿蒙的复合神名。
beats.textEn: Amun-Ra is registered as a syncretized expression involving Amun; the Amun entity remains independent.

deityStoryCards.name: Amun-Ra
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 阿蒙与太阳神拉的复合神祇档案；与阿蒙和拉各自的记录分开。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Composite deity dossier connecting Amun and Ra while preserving both component records.

beats.textZh: 阿蒙-拉在卡纳克阿蒙-拉大神庙受到崇拜。
beats.textEn: Archaeological project evidence attests a sanctuary dedicated to Amun-Ra at Karnak from the Middle Kingdom onward.
beats.sourceTitle: Karnak des origines: Middle Kingdom court and primeval temple

beats.textZh: 阿蒙-拉是包含阿蒙的复合神名。

beats.textZh: 阿蒙-拉的形象见于阿布辛贝。

deityStoryCards.name: Uranus
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《神谱》中由盖亚生出的星空之天，并为泰坦谱系的父辈。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Starry Heaven born from Gaia and parent in the Titan genealogy in the registered Hesiodic witness.

beats.textZh: 许珀里翁是乌拉诺斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 133-136 lists Hyperion among the children of Gaia and Uranus.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是乌拉诺斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 133-136 lists Theia among the children of Gaia and Uranus.

beats.textZh: 盖亚是乌拉诺斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 126-128 says Gaia bore starry Uranus equal to herself.

beats.textZh: 乌拉诺斯是克洛诺斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 133-138 includes Cronus among the children of Gaia and Uranus.

deityStoryCards.name: Nyx
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Night figure in Hesiodic genealogy, born from Chaos and parent of multiple personified powers in that witness.

beats.textZh: 埃忒耳是倪克斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 124-125 presents Aether as a child of Nyx.

beats.textZh: 赫墨拉是倪克斯的孩子。

beats.textZh: 塔纳托斯是倪克斯的孩子。

beats.textZh: 倪克斯象征夜。
beats.textEn: The comparative index connects Nyx with night while retaining the culture-specific deity record.

deityStoryCards.name: Crius
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 赫西俄德与《书库》谱系中的提坦神，与欧律比亚生下阿斯特赖俄斯、帕拉斯和提坦珀耳塞斯。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Titan in Hesiodic and Library genealogies, parent with Eurybia of Astraeus, Pallas and the Titan Perses.

beats.textZh: 克利俄斯是阿斯特赖俄斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Astraeus among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 克利俄斯是帕拉斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Pallas among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 克利俄斯是珀耳塞斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 and Library 1.2.2 make Crius a parent of the Titan Perses.

beats.textZh: 《神谱》的这一段把与克洛诺斯相连的泰坦置于宙斯及其盟友的对立面。
beats.textEn: This passage of the Theogony sets the Titans associated with Cronus against Zeus and his allies.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “泰坦战争”是现代通行事件名，见证范围仍指向原诗行。

beats.textZh: 宙斯是战斗的主要参与者；事件档案把雷、闪电和雷电武器记录为本段战斗手段，并记录百臂巨人的介入。
beats.textEn: Zeus is a principal combatant; the event profile records thunder, lightning, and the thunderbolt as weapons in this passage and records the intervention of the Hundred-Handers.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 没有把后世图像或现代叙事写入古诗。

beats.textZh: 在这一见证中，泰坦战败并被囚入塔耳塔罗斯；这项结果不自动代表所有古代作者的细节完全相同。
beats.textEn: In this witness, the Titans are defeated and confined in Tartarus; the result does not imply that every ancient author gives identical details.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 其他见证将在独立版本中比较。

facts.textZh: 赫斯提亚是克洛诺斯的孩子。

facts.textEn: Theogony 453-458 lists Hera among the children of Rhea and Cronus.

facts.textZh: 波塞冬是克洛诺斯的孩子。

facts.textZh: 盖亚是克洛诺斯的父母。

beats.textZh: 阿波罗是勒托的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Apollo as a child of Leto and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 阿耳忒弥斯是勒托的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Artemis as a child of Leto and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 勒托见于神谱。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: The first named cosmogonic condition or being in Hesiod’s Theogony; its ontology should not be flattened into the modern everyday sense of disorder.

beats.textEn: Theogony 371-374 presents Hyperion and Theia as parents of Eos.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是厄俄斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 371-374 presents Theia and Hyperion as parents of Eos.

beats.textZh: 赫利俄斯与厄俄斯是兄弟姐妹。

beats.textZh: 塞勒涅与厄俄斯是兄弟姐妹。

beats.textEn: Theogony 124-125 presents Erebus as Aether’s other parent.

beats.textZh: 厄瑞玻斯是卡俄斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 123 says Erebus arose from Chaos.

beats.textZh: 赫墨拉是厄瑞玻斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 124-125 presents Erebus as Hemera’s other parent.

deityStoryCards.name: Hades
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《神谱》家谱中的克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子；《荷马颂歌·致得墨忒耳》中的冥界统治者与劫掠者。

beats.textEn: The hymn opens with Persephone at the center of the taking to the underworld and says that Hades acts with the consent of Zeus in this witness.

beats.uncertaintyNote: 这里只陈述本赞歌的叙事，不代表所有希腊版本。

beats.textZh: 得墨忒耳离开诸神寻找女儿。赫卡忒与赫利俄斯出现在寻找段落中，承担的角色以已登记的赞歌行号为限。
beats.textEn: Demeter leaves the gods and searches for her daughter. Hecate and Helios appear in the search passage, with their roles limited to the registered hymn lines.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, Evelyn-White English text
beats.uncertaintyNote: 未把其他作者的寻找情节混入。

beats.textZh: 事件档案记录得墨忒耳来到厄琉息斯；赞歌继续处理珀耳塞福涅的回返安排及仪式建立。秘密仪式的内部内容没有从公开证据重构。
beats.textEn: The event record brings Demeter to Eleusis; the hymn continues with arrangements for Persephone to return and the establishment of rites. The internal content of the mysteries is not reconstructed from public evidence.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, Evelyn-White English text
beats.uncertaintyNote: 仪式内部内容明确保留为未知。

facts.textZh: 哈得斯是克洛诺斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 453-458 lists Hades among the children of Rhea and Cronus.

facts.textZh: 哈得斯是瑞亚的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 453-458 lists Hades among the children borne by Rhea to Cronus.

facts.textZh: 赫斯提亚与哈得斯是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Hestia and Hades occur among the children of Rhea and Cronus in Theogony 453-458.

deityStoryCards.name: Aether
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Aether is born from Nyx through union with Erebus in Theogony 124-125.

beats.textZh: 埃忒耳是厄瑞玻斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 124-125 presents Erebus as Aether’s other parent.

beats.textZh: 埃忒耳是倪克斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 124-125 presents Aether as a child of Nyx.

deityStoryCards.name: Thanatos
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Personified Death among the children of Nyx in Hesiod’s Theogony.

beats.textZh: 塔纳托斯是倪克斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 211-212 lists Thanatos among the children of Nyx.

beats.textZh: 塔纳托斯与许普诺斯是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Thanatos and Hypnos occur together as children of Nyx in the Hesiodic genealogy.

beats.textZh: 塔纳托斯象征死亡。
beats.textEn: The comparative index connects Thanatos with death while retaining the culture-specific deity record.

deityStoryCards.name: Selene
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Lunar deity, child of Hyperion and Theia in Hesiod and subject of Homeric Hymn 32.

beats.textZh: 塞勒涅——特征：radiant goddess driving shining horses and serving as a monthly sign
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 32 lines 1-20 describes Selene’s radiance, horses and monthly sign.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 32 to Selene, Evelyn-White edition and translation

beats.textZh: 许珀里翁是塞勒涅的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 371-374 presents Hyperion and Theia as parents of Selene.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是塞勒涅的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 371-374 presents Theia and Hyperion as parents of Selene.

beats.textZh: 赫利俄斯与塞勒涅是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Helios and Selene occur as children of Hyperion and Theia in Theogony 371-374.

beats.textZh: 塞勒涅与厄俄斯是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Selene and Eos occur as children of Hyperion and Theia in Theogony 371-374.

beats.textZh: 塞勒涅象征月亮。
beats.textEn: The comparative index connects Selene with the moon while retaining the Greek deity as a distinct entity.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 32 to Selene, Evelyn-White edition and translation

facts.textZh: 塞勒涅出现在《荷马颂歌·致塞勒涅》（第32首）中。
facts.textEn: Selene is the principal subject of Homeric Hymn 32.
facts.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 32 to Selene, Evelyn-White edition and translation

deityStoryCards.name: Semele
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 狄俄倪索斯的凡人母亲之一种古代叙事见证。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Mortal mother of Dionysus in the registered ancient witnesses.

beats.textZh: 狄俄倪索斯是塞墨勒的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 940-942 presents Dionysus as a child of Semele and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 塞墨勒见于神谱。
beats.textEn: Theogony 940-942 names Semele in the genealogy of Dionysus.

deityStoryCards.name: Metis
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Figure of wisdom in Hesiod, first consort of Zeus and mother of Athena in that witness.

beats.textZh: 墨提斯被宙斯囚禁。
beats.textEn: In Hesiod Zeus deceives Metis and puts her in his belly.

beats.textZh: 墨提斯——职掌：wisdom and counsel
beats.textEn: Theogony describes Metis as exceptionally wise and as devising good and evil for Zeus.

beats.textZh: 墨提斯是雅典娜的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony says Metis was about to give birth to Athena.

beats.textZh: 墨提斯与宙斯是配偶。
beats.textEn: Theogony calls Metis the first wife of Zeus.

beats.textZh: 墨提斯见于神谱。
beats.textEn: Metis appears in Theogony 886-900.

deityStoryCards.name: Zeus
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 希腊文本传统中的神王；当前页面分别连接雷霆、奥林匹亚、提丰之战和赫西俄德家谱证据。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Divine ruler in registered Greek textual and cult evidence.

beats.textZh: 《神谱》的这一段把与克洛诺斯相连的泰坦置于宙斯及其盟友的对立面。
beats.textEn: This passage of the Theogony sets the Titans associated with Cronus against Zeus and his allies.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “泰坦战争”是现代通行事件名，见证范围仍指向原诗行。

beats.textZh: 宙斯是战斗的主要参与者；事件档案把雷、闪电和雷电武器记录为本段战斗手段，并记录百臂巨人的介入。
beats.textEn: Zeus is a principal combatant; the event profile records thunder, lightning, and the thunderbolt as weapons in this passage and records the intervention of the Hundred-Handers.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 没有把后世图像或现代叙事写入古诗。

beats.textZh: 在这一见证中，泰坦战败并被囚入塔耳塔罗斯；这项结果不自动代表所有古代作者的细节完全相同。
beats.textEn: In this witness, the Titans are defeated and confined in Tartarus; the result does not imply that every ancient author gives identical details.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 其他见证将在独立版本中比较。

facts.textZh: 阿佛洛狄忒是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Iliad 14 refers to Aphrodite as a daughter of Zeus.

facts.textZh: 阿波罗是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Apollo as a child of Leto and Zeus.

facts.textZh: 阿瑞斯是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 921-923 presents Ares among the children of Hera and Zeus.

facts.textZh: 阿耳忒弥斯是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Artemis as a child of Leto and Zeus.

facts.textZh: 雅典娜是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 924-926 describes Athena as produced from Zeus’s head.

facts.textZh: 狄俄倪索斯是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 940-942 presents Dionysus as a child of Semele and Zeus.

deityStoryCards.name: Pallas (Titan)
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 克利俄斯与欧律比亚之子；以限定 ID 与其他名为帕拉斯的神话人物分开。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Crius and Eurybia; scoped ID prevents merger with other figures named Pallas.

beats.textZh: 克利俄斯是帕拉斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Pallas among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 欧律比亚是帕拉斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Pallas among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）与帕拉斯（提坦）是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 lists Perses and Pallas as children of Crius and Eurybia.

deityStoryCards.name: Demeter
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 克洛诺斯与瑞亚之女、珀耳塞福涅之母；第2首颂歌连接寻找女儿与厄琉西斯仪式叙事。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Cronus and Rhea and mother of Persephone in registered witnesses.

beats.textZh: 赞歌开篇把珀耳塞福涅置于被带往冥界的事件中心，并说哈得斯在本见证中得到宙斯同意。
beats.textEn: The hymn opens with Persephone at the center of the taking to the underworld and says that Hades acts with the consent of Zeus in this witness.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, Evelyn-White English text
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这里只陈述本赞歌的叙事，不代表所有希腊版本。

beats.textZh: 得墨忒耳离开诸神寻找女儿。赫卡忒与赫利俄斯出现在寻找段落中，承担的角色以已登记的赞歌行号为限。
beats.textEn: Demeter leaves the gods and searches for her daughter. Hecate and Helios appear in the search passage, with their roles limited to the registered hymn lines.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, Evelyn-White English text
beats.uncertaintyNote: 未把其他作者的寻找情节混入。

beats.textZh: 事件档案记录得墨忒耳来到厄琉息斯；赞歌继续处理珀耳塞福涅的回返安排及仪式建立。秘密仪式的内部内容没有从公开证据重构。
beats.textEn: The event record brings Demeter to Eleusis; the hymn continues with arrangements for Persephone to return and the establishment of rites. The internal content of the mysteries is not reconstructed from public evidence.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, Evelyn-White English text
beats.uncertaintyNote: 仪式内部内容明确保留为未知。

facts.textZh: 得墨忒耳是克洛诺斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 453-458 lists Demeter among the children of Rhea and Cronus.

facts.textZh: 得墨忒耳是瑞亚的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 453-458 lists Demeter among the children borne by Rhea to Cronus.

facts.textZh: 珀耳塞福涅是得墨忒耳的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 912-914 presents Persephone as a child of Demeter and Zeus.

facts.textZh: 赫斯提亚与得墨忒耳是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Hestia and Demeter occur among the children of Rhea and Cronus in Theogony 453-458.

facts.textZh: 得墨忒耳在厄琉息斯受到崇拜。
facts.textEn: The official archaeological record identifies Eleusis as the sanctuary of Demeter and Kore.

facts.textZh: 得墨忒耳与厄琉息斯相关。
facts.textEn: Homeric Hymn 2 places Demeter’s arrival and the establishment of rites at Eleusis.
facts.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Theia
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Titan child of Gaia and Uranus and parent, with Hyperion, of Helios, Selene and Eos in Hesiod.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是盖亚的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 133-136 lists Theia among the children of Gaia and Uranus.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是乌拉诺斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 133-136 lists Theia among the children of Gaia and Uranus.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是厄俄斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 371-374 presents Theia and Hyperion as parents of Eos.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是赫利俄斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 371-374 presents Theia and Hyperion as parents of Helios.

beats.textZh: 忒亚是塞勒涅的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 371-374 presents Theia and Hyperion as parents of Selene.

deityStoryCards.name: Eurybia
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 与克利俄斯生下阿斯特赖俄斯、帕拉斯和提坦珀耳塞斯的女神；与其他同名人物分开。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Goddess paired with Crius in the genealogy of Astraeus, Pallas and the Titan Perses.

beats.textZh: 欧律比亚是阿斯特赖俄斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Astraeus among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 欧律比亚是帕拉斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Pallas among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 欧律比亚是珀耳塞斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 and Library 1.2.2 make Eurybia a parent of the Titan Perses.

deityStoryCards.name: Poseidon
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《神谱》家谱中的克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子；第22首《荷马颂歌》联系大地、海洋、马与船。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Cronus and Rhea; linked with earth, sea, horses and ships in Hymn 22.

beats.textZh: 波塞冬——职掌：earth, sea, horses and ships in Homeric Hymn 22
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 22 links Poseidon with earth, sea, horses and the saving of ships.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 22 to Poseidon, Evelyn-White English text

beats.textZh: 波塞冬是克洛诺斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 453-458 lists Poseidon among the children of Rhea and Cronus.

beats.textZh: 波塞冬是瑞亚的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 453-458 lists Poseidon among the children borne by Rhea to Cronus.

beats.textZh: 赫斯提亚与波塞冬是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Hestia and Poseidon occur among the children of Rhea and Cronus in Theogony 453-458.

beats.textZh: 波塞冬使用波塞冬三叉戟。
beats.textEn: Poseidon is identified iconographically by the trident.
beats.sourceTitle: Bronze statuette of Zeus or Poseidon

beats.textZh: 宙斯或波塞冬青铜像描绘了波塞冬。
beats.textEn: The bronze statuette may depict Poseidon if its lost attribute was a trident.
beats.sourceTitle: Bronze statuette of Zeus or Poseidon

facts.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致波塞冬》（第22首）提到波塞冬。
facts.textEn: Homeric Hymn 22 is addressed to Poseidon.
facts.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 22 to Poseidon, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Dionysus
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 宙斯与塞墨勒之子；第7首《荷马颂歌》保存海盗事件的神话叙事。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Zeus and Semele; Hymn 7 preserves the pirate episode.

beats.textZh: 狄俄倪索斯——角色：divine protagonist of the pirate episode in Homeric Hymn 7
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 7 narrates pirates seizing Dionysus and the ensuing divine epiphany.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 7 to Dionysus, Evelyn-White English text

beats.textZh: 狄俄倪索斯是塞墨勒的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 940-942 presents Dionysus as a child of Semele and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 狄俄倪索斯是宙斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 940-942 presents Dionysus as a child of Semele and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致狄俄倪索斯》（第7首）提到狄俄倪索斯。
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 7 narrates Dionysus’s encounter with pirates.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 7 to Dionysus, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Dione
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《伊利亚特》第5卷称阿佛洛狄忒投入其母狄俄涅怀中；该谱系与赫西俄德起源叙事并存。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: The Iliad names Dione as Aphrodite’s mother; this coexists with the Hesiodic origin account.

beats.textZh: 《伊利亚特》第5卷写阿佛洛狄忒来到母亲狄俄涅身边。这是亲属称谓见证，不是完整诞生场景。
beats.textEn: Iliad Book 5 presents Aphrodite coming to her mother Dione. This is a kinship witness, not a complete birth scene.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不要从一处称谓推演未叙述的出生过程。

beats.textZh: 《伊利亚特》第14卷又把阿佛洛狄忒称为宙斯之女，形成与《神谱》海中诞生不同的家谱层。
beats.textEn: Iliad Book 14 also calls Aphrodite a daughter of Zeus, creating a genealogical layer different from the sea-birth account in the Theogony.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “女儿”是文本称谓；本页不补写其出生情节。

beats.textZh: 数据库保留《神谱》与《伊利亚特》的差异，并通过冲突档案让读者并排查看，而不是按名称或现代常识合并。
beats.textEn: The database preserves the difference between the Theogony and the Iliad and exposes it through a conflict record instead of merging the accounts by name or modern convention.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 冲突状态保持开放。

deityStoryCards.name: Perses (Titan)
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 赫西俄德与《书库》中克利俄斯、欧律比亚之子，阿斯特赖俄斯与帕拉斯之兄弟，阿斯忒里亚的配偶及赫卡忒之父。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Titan son of Crius and Eurybia, brother of Astraeus and Pallas, consort of Asteria and father of Hecate.

beats.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）是赫卡忒的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 404-409 presents Perses and Asteria as parents of Hecate.

beats.textZh: 克利俄斯是珀耳塞斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 and Library 1.2.2 make Crius a parent of the Titan Perses.

beats.textZh: 欧律比亚是珀耳塞斯（提坦）的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 and Library 1.2.2 make Eurybia a parent of the Titan Perses.

beats.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）是赫卡忒的父母。
beats.textEn: Library 1.2.4 makes Hecate the child of Perses and Asteria.

beats.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）与阿斯特赖俄斯是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 lists Perses and Astraeus as children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）与帕拉斯（提坦）是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 lists Perses and Pallas as children of Crius and Eurybia.

facts.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）与阿斯忒里亚是配偶。
facts.textEn: Theogony 404-410 says Asteria became the wife of this Perses and bore Hecate.

facts.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）见于伪阿波罗多洛斯《书库》。
facts.textEn: Library 1.2.2-1.2.4 presents Perses as son of Crius and Eurybia and father of Hecate.

facts.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）见于神谱。
facts.textEn: The Titan Perses appears in the continuous genealogy at Theogony 375-410.

deityStoryCards.nameZh: 珀耳塞斯（赫利俄斯之子）
deityStoryCards.name: Perses (son of Helios)
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 狄奥多罗斯与《书库》科尔喀斯叙事中的珀耳塞斯，赫利俄斯之子、埃厄忒斯之兄弟；不是赫卡忒之父。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Colchian Perses, son of Helios and brother of Aeetes; not the father of Hecate.

beats.textZh: 《书库》1.9.28把美狄亚写成返回科尔喀斯并采取行动的人物。
beats.textEn: Library 1.9.28 presents Medea as the figure who returns to Colchis and acts.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是汇编中的短序列，不扩写对话或动机。

beats.textZh: 在这一段中，被杀并被废黜的是赫利俄斯之子、埃厄忒斯兄弟的珀耳塞斯，而不是赫卡忒之父的泰坦珀耳塞斯。
beats.textEn: The Perses killed and deposed here is the son of Helios and brother of Aeetes, not the Titan Perses who is father of Hecate.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 严格防止同名人物合并。

beats.textZh: 短篇以埃厄忒斯恢复王位结束；当前证据没有为这一结局补写更长的政治过程。
beats.textEn: The short sequence ends with Aeetes restored to the kingdom; the current evidence does not invent a longer political process.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前证据未说明的过程保持空缺。

facts.textZh: 赫利俄斯是珀耳塞斯（赫利俄斯之子）的父母。
facts.textEn: Diodorus 4.45.1 names Helios as father of a different Perses in the Colchian/Tauric narrative.
facts.sourceTitle: Diodorus Siculus, Library of History, Book 4.45.1

facts.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（赫利俄斯之子）与埃厄忒斯是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Diodorus 4.45.1 presents Aeetes and Perses as sons of Helios.
facts.sourceTitle: Diodorus Siculus, Library of History, Book 4.45.1

facts.textZh: 美狄亚杀死了珀耳塞斯（赫利俄斯之子）。
facts.textEn: Library 1.9.28 says Medea killed the Perses who had deposed Aeetes.

facts.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（赫利俄斯之子）击败了埃厄忒斯。
facts.textEn: Library 1.9.28 says Perses had deposed his brother Aeetes.

facts.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（赫利俄斯之子）见于伪阿波罗多洛斯《书库》。

facts.textZh: 阿佛洛狄忒是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Iliad 14 refers to Aphrodite as a daughter of Zeus.

facts.textZh: 阿佛洛狄忒是狄俄涅的孩子。
facts.textEn: Iliad 5 describes Aphrodite falling into the lap of her mother Dione.

facts.textZh: 阿佛洛狄忒在达夫尼阿佛洛狄忒圣所受到崇拜。
facts.textEn: Offerings and inscriptions identify worship of Aphrodite at the Daphne sanctuary.
facts.sourceLocation: Official object, site or museum record cited in claim notes

facts.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致阿佛洛狄忒》（第5首）提到阿佛洛狄忒。
facts.textEn: Homeric Hymn 5 is addressed to Aphrodite.
facts.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 5 to Aphrodite, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Asteria
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Parent of Hecate with Perses in Hesiod’s Theogony.

beats.textZh: 阿斯忒里亚是赫卡忒的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 404-409 presents Asteria and Perses as parents of Hecate.

beats.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）与阿斯忒里亚是配偶。
beats.textEn: Theogony 404-410 says Asteria became the wife of this Perses and bore Hecate.

deityStoryCards.name: Astraeus
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 克利俄斯与欧律比亚之子，提坦珀耳塞斯和帕拉斯的兄弟。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Crius and Eurybia, brother of the Titan Perses and Pallas.

beats.textZh: 克利俄斯是阿斯特赖俄斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Astraeus among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 欧律比亚是阿斯特赖俄斯的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 names Astraeus among the children of Crius and Eurybia.

beats.textZh: 珀耳塞斯（提坦）与阿斯特赖俄斯是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Theogony 375-377 lists Perses and Astraeus as children of Crius and Eurybia.

deityStoryCards.name: Apollo
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 勒托与宙斯之子；第3首《荷马颂歌》连接提洛岛诞生、弓、琴与神谕。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Leto and Zeus; Hymn 3 connects his Delian birth, bow, lyre and oracle.

beats.textZh: 阿波罗诞生于提洛岛。
beats.textEn: Greek myth locates Apollo's birth on Delos.

beats.textZh: 阿波罗是勒托的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Apollo as a child of Leto and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 阿波罗是宙斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Apollo as a child of Leto and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 阿波罗使用阿波罗之弓。
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 3 repeatedly characterizes Apollo as bearing or delighting in the bow.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 3 to Apollo, Evelyn-White English text

beats.textZh: 阿波罗在德尔斐受到崇拜。
beats.textEn: Delphi was the pan-Hellenic sanctuary where Apollo's oracle spoke.

beats.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致阿波罗》（第3首）提到阿波罗。
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 3 is addressed to Apollo and narrates major Delian and Pythian episodes.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 3 to Apollo, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Ares
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 宙斯与赫拉之子；第8首颂歌同时保存武力称号与克制、和平祈愿。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Zeus and Hera; Hymn 8 combines martial titles with a prayer for restraint.

beats.textZh: 阿瑞斯——职掌：martial force coupled with a closing prayer for restraint and peace
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 8 gives Ares martial titles but closes by asking for courage, restraint and peace.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 8 to Ares, Evelyn-White edition

beats.textZh: 阿瑞斯是赫拉的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 921-923 presents Ares among the children of Hera and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 阿瑞斯是宙斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 921-923 presents Ares among the children of Hera and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致阿瑞斯》（第8首）提到阿瑞斯。
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 8 is addressed to Ares.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 8 to Ares, Evelyn-White edition

deityStoryCards.name: Artemis
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 勒托与宙斯之女；第27首《荷马颂歌》描绘其弓箭、猎犬、鹿与阿波罗关系。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Leto and Zeus; Hymn 27 depicts archery, hounds and deer.

beats.textZh: 阿耳忒弥斯是勒托的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Artemis as a child of Leto and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 阿耳忒弥斯是宙斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 918-920 presents Artemis as a child of Leto and Zeus.

beats.textZh: 阿耳忒弥斯使用阿耳忒弥斯之弓。
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 27 portrays Artemis as a golden-shafted archer hunting deer.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 27 to Artemis, Evelyn-White English text

beats.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致阿耳忒弥斯》（第27首）提到阿耳忒弥斯。
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 27 is addressed to Artemis.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 27 to Artemis, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Athena
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 赫西俄德与颂歌传统中从宙斯而生、具武装与城邦守护层面的女神；埃癸斯证据另接《伊利亚特》。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Armed daughter of Zeus and city guardian in registered witnesses.

beats.textZh: 雅典娜是宙斯的孩子。
beats.textEn: Theogony 924-926 describes Athena as produced from Zeus’s head.

beats.textZh: 墨提斯是雅典娜的父母。
beats.textEn: Theogony says Metis was about to give birth to Athena.

beats.textZh: 雅典娜使用埃癸斯神盾。
beats.textEn: Iliad 5 depicts Athena putting on the tasselled aegis while arming for battle.

beats.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致雅典娜》（第28首）提到雅典娜。
beats.textEn: Homeric Hymn 28 is addressed to Athena and narrates her armed birth.
beats.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 28 to Athena, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Indra
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《梨俱吠陀》中的因陀罗：金刚杵持有者，并在 1.32 与 2.12 的具体见证中与蛇敌、受阻水流、大气和战斗相连。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Indra in registered Rigvedic witnesses, wielder of the vajra and linked to serpent combat, released waters, atmosphere and battle.

beats.textZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32把因陀罗列为主要行动者，把弗栗多列为他的对手。
beats.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 identifies Indra as the principal agent and Vrtra as his opponent.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 本页只代表此颂歌见证。

beats.textZh: 同一颂歌的登记Claims把金刚杵连接到因陀罗，并把其制造连接到陀湿多。
beats.textEn: Claims registered from the same hymn connect the vajra to Indra and its making to Tvastr.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把后期佛教或图像版本反投到吠陀颂歌。

beats.textZh: 事件档案以对手被击杀、水得以流出作为颂歌叙事结果；它不是现代自然科学陈述。
beats.textEn: The event profile records the opponent struck down and the waters flowing out as the narrative result of the hymn; it is not a modern scientific statement.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 知识层保持为神话叙事／文本见证。

facts.textZh: 因陀罗使用金刚杵／雷霆。
facts.textEn: In RV 1.32, Indra is associated with wielding the vajra against Vṛtra.
facts.sourceLocation: Registered text passage or museum catalogue

facts.textZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32见证提到因陀罗。
facts.textEn: RV 1.32 names Indra as the hymn’s deity and actor.
facts.sourceLocation: Registered text passage or museum catalogue

facts.textZh: 因陀罗杀死了弗栗多。
facts.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 narrates Indra killing Vrtra, also designated as a serpent in the hymn.

facts.textZh: 因陀罗与雷相关。
facts.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 places Indra’s combat amid lightning, thunder and rain imagery while preserving its own Vedic vocabulary and narrative.

deityStoryCards.name: Tvastr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32 见证中为因陀罗制作金刚杵者。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Maker of Indra’s vajra in the registered Rigveda 1.32 witness.

beats.textZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32把因陀罗列为主要行动者，把弗栗多列为他的对手。
beats.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 identifies Indra as the principal agent and Vrtra as his opponent.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 本页只代表此颂歌见证。

beats.textZh: 同一颂歌的登记Claims把金刚杵连接到因陀罗，并把其制造连接到陀湿多。
beats.textEn: Claims registered from the same hymn connect the vajra to Indra and its making to Tvastr.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把后期佛教或图像版本反投到吠陀颂歌。

beats.textZh: 事件档案以对手被击杀、水得以流出作为颂歌叙事结果；它不是现代自然科学陈述。
beats.textEn: The event profile records the opponent struck down and the waters flowing out as the narrative result of the hymn; it is not a modern scientific statement.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 知识层保持为神话叙事／文本见证。

facts.textZh: 陀湿多创造了金刚杵／雷霆。
facts.textEn: Rigveda 1.32.2 says Tvastr fashioned the vajra for Indra.

deityStoryCards.name: Tlaloc
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 与农业相关的雨神；大神庙北侧是他的神庙（墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Rain god linked to agriculture whose temple occupied the north side of the Templo Mayor (INAH).

beats.headingEn: The war god on the south
beats.textZh: 大神庙南侧的神殿属于维齐洛波奇特利——墨西加人的太阳战神，也是他们的守护神。
beats.textEn: The southern chapel of the Templo Mayor belongs to Huitzilopochtli, the Mexica's solar god of war and their patron.
beats.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor

beats.headingEn: The rain god on the north
beats.textZh: 北侧的神殿属于特拉洛克——掌管雨水、与农业紧密相连的神。战争与农业，两位神并立在同一座金字塔的顶端。
beats.textEn: The northern temple belongs to Tlaloc, god of rain and closely tied to agriculture. War and farming stand side by side at the top of one pyramid.
beats.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor

beats.headingEn: A temple that grew in layers
beats.textZh: 据 INAH 介绍，墨西加人在1325年建立特诺奇蒂特兰时修了一座小神庙，此后经过多次重建和扩建，越修越高。
beats.textEn: According to INAH, the Mexica built a small temple when they founded Tenochtitlan in 1325, and it was rebuilt and enlarged many times over.
beats.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor
beats.uncertaintyNote: 各建造阶段的具体年代仍有不确定之处。

facts.textZh: 特拉洛克——职掌：rain and agriculture
facts.textEn: INAH calls Tlaloc the god of rain, directly linked to agriculture.
facts.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor

deityStoryCards.name: Tezcatlipoca
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 又称蒂特拉卡瓦；《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷中令羽蛇神在图拉衰落的巫师之一。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Also called Titlacauan; among the sorcerers who bring Quetzalcoatl's glory at Tollan to an end (Florentine Codex Book 3).

beats.headingZh: 被当作神的蒂特拉卡瓦
beats.headingEn: Titlacauan, held to be a god
beats.textZh: 第三卷第2章讲人们怎样把一位叫蒂特拉卡瓦、也叫特斯卡特利波卡的人物当作神来敬奉。
beats.textEn: Chapter 2 of Book 3 tells how one called Titlacauan, or Tezcatlipoca, came to be regarded as a god.

beats.textZh: 第3章讲羽蛇神——图拉的一位大法师。第4章说，当巫师们来到他身边，他的荣光便走到了尽头；第5章又记下蒂特拉卡瓦带来的另一个异兆。
beats.textEn: Chapter 3 tells of Quetzalcoatl, a great wizard at Tollan. Chapter 4 relates how his glory came to an end when the sorcerers came to him, and chapter 5 records another portent brought about by Titlacauan.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 本段依据章节标题与概要，具体情节尚未逐句核对。

beats.textZh: 第14章记载，羽蛇神离去时，追随他的人经过伊斯塔克特佩特尔与波波卡特佩特尔两座雪山之间，被冻死在冰雪里。
beats.textEn: Chapter 14 records that as Quetzalcoatl departs, his vassals freeze to death in the ice as they pass between Iztactepetl and Popocatepetl.

facts.textZh: 特斯卡特利波卡出现在“羽蛇神在图拉的衰落”之中。
facts.textEn: Titlacauan is among the sorcerers whose portents bring Quetzalcoatl's glory to an end (Book 3, chapters 4–5).

deityStoryCards.name: Coyolxauhqui
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Coatlicue who leads her brothers against their mother and is killed by Huitzilopochtli at Coatepec.

beats.textZh: 科阿特利库埃住在蛇山上。一天她打扫时，一团羽毛从天上飘下来。她把羽毛捡起来，塞在腰间——就这样怀孕了。
beats.textEn: Coatlicue lives on Coatepec. One day as she sweeps, a ball of feathers drifts down. She picks it up and tucks it at her waist — and so she becomes pregnant.

beats.textZh: 她的女儿科约尔沙乌基对兄弟们——四百个南方人——说：母亲让我们蒙羞，我们必须杀了她。于是他们全副武装，朝蛇山进发。
beats.textEn: Her daughter Coyolxauhqui tells her brothers, the four hundred Centzon Huitznahua, that their mother has shamed them and must be killed. Armed, they set out for Coatepec.

beats.textZh: 腹中的维齐洛波奇特利安慰母亲：不要怕，我知道该怎么做。敌人冲上山顶的那一刻，他出生了，手持盾牌、投枪和投枪器。
beats.textEn: From the womb Huitzilopochtli comforts his mother: do not be afraid, I know what to do. The moment the attackers reach the summit he is born, carrying shield, darts and dart-thrower.

beats.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，她的身体沿着蛇山滚落下去。四百个兄弟也被他从山顶追得四散奔逃。
beats.textEn: Huitzilopochtli cuts off Coyolxauhqui's head, and her body tumbles down the side of Coatepec. He drives the four hundred brothers from the summit, scattering them in every direction.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 学者认为这段叙事与大神庙的布局相呼应，属于解释，不写成事实。

facts.textZh: 科约尔沙乌基是科阿特利库埃的孩子。
facts.textEn: Coyolxauhqui is a daughter of Coatlicue who urges her brothers, the Centzon Huitznahua, to kill their mother.

facts.textEn: Huitzilopochtli is the child Coatlicue conceives at Coatepec.

facts.textEn: INAH calls Huitzilopochtli the solar god of war and patron of the Mexica.

facts.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利是科阿特利库埃的孩子。
facts.textEn: Huitzilopochtli is the child Coatlicue conceives at Coatepec.

facts.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利在特诺奇蒂特兰大神庙受到崇拜。
facts.textEn: INAH describes Huitzilopochtli's chapel on the south side of the Templo Mayor.

facts.textEn: He scatters the Centzon Huitznahua from the top of Coatepec.

deityStoryCards.name: Quetzalcoatl
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷中图拉的大法师，巫师们到来后他的荣光走向终结。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Great wizard of Tollan whose glory ends when sorcerers come to him in Florentine Codex Book 3.

beats.headingZh: 被当作神的蒂特拉卡瓦
beats.headingEn: Titlacauan, held to be a god
beats.textZh: 第三卷第2章讲人们怎样把一位叫蒂特拉卡瓦、也叫特斯卡特利波卡的人物当作神来敬奉。
beats.textEn: Chapter 2 of Book 3 tells how one called Titlacauan, or Tezcatlipoca, came to be regarded as a god.

beats.textZh: 第3章讲羽蛇神——图拉的一位大法师。第4章说，当巫师们来到他身边，他的荣光便走到了尽头；第5章又记下蒂特拉卡瓦带来的另一个异兆。
beats.textEn: Chapter 3 tells of Quetzalcoatl, a great wizard at Tollan. Chapter 4 relates how his glory came to an end when the sorcerers came to him, and chapter 5 records another portent brought about by Titlacauan.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 本段依据章节标题与概要，具体情节尚未逐句核对。

beats.textZh: 第14章记载，羽蛇神离去时，追随他的人经过伊斯塔克特佩特尔与波波卡特佩特尔两座雪山之间，被冻死在冰雪里。
beats.textEn: Chapter 14 records that as Quetzalcoatl departs, his vassals freeze to death in the ice as they pass between Iztactepetl and Popocatepetl.

facts.textZh: 羽蛇神——描述：a great wizard of Tollan
facts.textEn: Book 3, chapter 3 tells the tale of Quetzalcoatl as a great wizard of Tollan.

facts.textZh: 库库尔坎 · name translation of · 羽蛇神
facts.textEn: UNESCO reports, as the most common version, that the Tula ruler Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl was called Kukulkan as the Maya translated the name.

deityStoryCards.name: Pele
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 夏威夷火山之神；据美国国家公园管理局对口述传统的概述，她从卡希基远航而来，定居基拉韦厄的哈雷茂茂火山口。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Hawaiian volcano deity who, in NPS's summary of oral history, voyaged from Kahiki and made her home in Halemaʻumaʻu crater at Kīlauea.

beats.textZh: 国家公园管理局介绍说，按照口述传统，佩蕾是夏威夷的火山之神，是一股自然之力，也是这些火山地貌的创造者。她出生在遥远的卡希基，为了给自己的火和家人寻找合适的家，乘船来到夏威夷群岛。
beats.textEn: The National Park Service explains that, in oral history, Pele is the Hawaiian volcano deity, an elemental force and the creator of these volcanic landscapes. Born in the distant land of Kahiki, she voyaged to the Hawaiian Islands to find a suitable home for her fire and family.

beats.headingEn: Island by island to the southeast
beats.textZh: 她一座岛一座岛地向东南迁移，寻找能安顿下来的地方。
beats.textEn: She moved southeast through the islands, one after another, looking for a place to settle.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 各岛上的具体经历因版本而异，本站不补写。

beats.textZh: 最后她来到基拉韦厄山顶的哈雷茂茂火山口，把这里定为永久的家。据说她至今仍住在那里。
beats.textEn: At last she came to Halemaʻumaʻu crater at the summit of Kīlauea and made it her permanent home. She is said to live there still.

beats.textZh: 在夏威夷传统中，经过佩蕾的土地要先请求她的许可。国家公园管理局也请访客在这片神圣的地景中保持尊重。公园还提醒：不同的 moʻolelo 版本可能差别很大。
beats.textEn: In Hawaiian tradition it is customary to ask Pele's permission to travel through her land, and the park asks visitors to behave respectfully in this sacred landscape. It also notes that versions of the moʻolelo may differ, sometimes greatly.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这里只讲公开概述；家族与地方传统不在收集范围。

facts.textZh: 佩蕾——职掌：volcanoes; elemental force; creator of volcanic landscapes
facts.textEn: NPS describes Pele as the Hawaiian volcano deity, an elemental force and the creator of the volcanic landscapes.

beats.headingEn: The two sides of the creation combat
beats.textZh: 登记的《埃努玛·埃利什》Claims确认马尔杜克与提亚马特都参与这场创世战斗。
beats.textEn: Registered Enuma elish claims confirm that both Marduk and Tiamat participate in the creation combat.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 战斗逐步过程尚未入库。

beats.textZh: 故事页直接连接电子巴比伦图书馆的数字语料，而不是引用无出处的现代故事改写。
beats.textEn: The story page links directly to the electronic Babylonian Library corpus instead of relying on an unsourced modern retelling.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 语料界面与翻译权利按来源条款。

beats.textZh: 胜负、世界形成与王权确认的详细次序将在泥板逐行建模后加入；当前不把常见概述冒充已验证Claims。
beats.textEn: The detailed order of victory, world formation, and kingship will be added after tablet-level modeling; common summaries are not presented as verified claims here.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前证据未细分这些阶段。

facts.textZh: 马尔杜克击败了提亚马特。
facts.textEn: In Enūma eliš, Marduk defeats Tiamat.

facts.textEn: In Enūma eliš Tablet IV, Marduk fashions and uses a bow.

facts.textZh: 马尔杜克使用马尔杜克之网。
facts.textEn: In Enūma eliš Tablet IV, Marduk uses a net against Tiamat.

facts.textZh: 马尔杜克击败了提亚马特。
facts.textEn: In Enūma eliš, Marduk defeats Tiamat.

deityStoryCards.name: Perun
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《往年纪事》所见东斯拉夫佩伦：条约誓言、980 年基辅神像与 988 年毁像分别登记；“全斯拉夫唯一主神”与命名神器不作无证断言。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Perun in East Slavic chronicle witnesses: treaty oaths, the 980 Kyiv idol and its 988 removal are separate claims; no unsupported universal pantheon or named weapon is asserted.

beats.textZh: 《往年纪事》980 年条记载：弗拉基米尔开始在基辅独自为王，就在宫殿庭院外的山岗上立起一排神像。
beats.textEn: The Primary Chronicle's annal for 980 records that when Volodimer began to reign alone in Kyiv, he set up a row of idols on the hill outside the palace courtyard.
beats.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition

beats.textZh: 最前面的是佩伦：木头雕成，头是银的，胡须是金的。
beats.textEn: First stood Perun, carved of wood, with a silver head and a golden moustache.
beats.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition

beats.headingEn: Mokosh at the end of the list
beats.textZh: 接下来是霍尔斯、达日博格、斯特里博格、西马尔格尔，名单的最后一位是莫科什。人们向这些神像献上祭品。编年史只记下了莫科什的名字，没有说她掌管什么。
beats.textEn: Then came Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog and Simargl, and last on the list, Mokosh. People brought offerings to the idols. The chronicle records only Mokosh's name, not what she governed.
beats.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition
beats.uncertaintyNote: 关于莫科什职能的说法来自其他材料与现代研究，本故事不补写。

beats.textZh: 八年后，弗拉基米尔受洗，下令推倒这些神像：有的砍碎，有的烧掉。佩伦被绑在马尾上拖下山，有人用棍子抽打，最后被扔进第聂伯河。
beats.textEn: Eight years later Volodimer was baptized and ordered the idols overthrown — some cut to pieces, others burned. Perun was tied to a horse's tail and dragged down the hill, beaten with sticks, and thrown into the Dnieper.
beats.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是皈依一方的记载，不是对斯拉夫宗教的中立描述。

facts.textZh: 佩伦与维列斯一同被呼告。
facts.textEn: The 907 and 971 treaty-oath traditions invoke Perun and Veles or Volos together.
facts.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition

facts.textZh: 佩伦与980 年基辅山岗神像相关。
facts.textEn: Perun heads the 980 list of idols on the Kyiv hill.
facts.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition

facts.textZh: 佩伦出现在往年纪事中。
facts.textEn: The Primary Chronicle names Perun in treaty-oath entries and in the 980 and 988 Kyiv idol episodes.
facts.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition

facts.textZh: 佩伦与雷相关。
facts.textEn: Modern academic reference contextualizes the chronicle’s Perun as an East Slavic thunder and lightning deity.

beats.textZh: 佩伦与维列斯一同被呼告。
beats.textEn: The 907 and 971 treaty-oath traditions invoke Perun and Veles or Volos together.
beats.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Named last among the idols Volodimer set up on the Kyiv hill in the Primary Chronicle's annal for 980; no function is stated there.

facts.textEn: Mokosh is one of the idols Volodimer sets up on the Kyiv hill, to which people make offerings.
facts.sourceTitle: Tale of Bygone Years digital critical edition

deityStoryCards.name: Izanagi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》中的男性创世神：与伊邪那美造出淤能碁吕岛，追往黄泉，归来禊祓时生出天照大神、月读与须佐之男。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Male creator deity of the Kojiki: with Izanami he forms Onogoro Island, follows her to Yomi, and on returning gives birth to Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi and Susanoo as he purifies himself.

beats.headingEn: A spear from the Floating Bridge
beats.textZh: 天上的众神命令伊邪那岐和伊邪那美去巩固还在漂浮的大地，并交给他们一支镶玉的天沼矛。两神站在天浮桥上，把矛伸进海里搅动；提起矛时，矛尖滴下的盐水层层堆积，成了淤能碁吕岛。
beats.textEn: The heavenly deities command Izanagi and Izanami to make firm the drifting land and give them a jewelled spear. Standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, they stir the brine; when they lift the spear, the drops from its tip pile up into Onogoro Island.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 《日本书纪》说两神是自己决定动手，本版不合并。

beats.headingEn: The birth of the fire deity
beats.textZh: 两神结合，生出许多岛屿和神灵。可是伊邪那美生下火神时被烧伤，病倒在床，最终“神去”——也就是死去。
beats.textEn: Joined together, the pair bring forth islands and deities. But when Izanami gives birth to the Deity-of-Fire she is burned, falls sick, and at length 'divinely retires' — she dies.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)

beats.textZh: 伊邪那岐想再见到妻子，便追到黄泉，请她回去：“我们造的国土还没有完成。”伊邪那美回答：你来得太晚了，我已经吃了黄泉灶火煮的东西——不过她答应去和黄泉的神商量。
beats.textEn: Longing to see her, Izanagi follows Izanami to Yomi and asks her to come back, for the lands they made are not yet finished. She answers that he has come too late: she has already eaten from the hearth of Yomi — yet she agrees to consult the deities there.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 之后的逃离情节可参看本库“黄泉中的八雷神”故事。

beats.textZh: 伊邪那岐回来后在水中洗净自己，身上不断化生出神。最后，他洗左眼时生出天照大神，洗右眼时生出月读，洗鼻子时生出须佐之男。
beats.textEn: Back from Yomi, Izanagi bathes to purify himself, and deities are born as he washes. Last of all, washing his left eye brings forth Amaterasu, his right eye Tsukuyomi, and his nose Susanoo.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 三神的通行名称来自译者注释。

facts.textZh: 天照大神是伊邪那岐的孩子。
facts.textEn: The deity born when Izanagi washes his left eye is rendered by Chamberlain as Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.
facts.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
facts.sourceLocation: Sect. X, Purification of the August Person (kj017)

facts.textZh: 须佐之男是伊邪那岐的孩子。
facts.textEn: The deity born when Izanagi washes his nose is rendered by Chamberlain as His Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness.
facts.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
facts.sourceLocation: Sect. X, Purification of the August Person (kj017)

facts.textZh: 伊邪那岐与伊邪那美是配偶。
facts.textEn: Izanagi and Izanami court each other and produce the islands and deities in the Kojiki.
facts.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
facts.sourceLocation: Sect. IV–V, courtship and the birth of the islands

facts.textZh: 伊邪那岐出现在“淤能碁吕岛的形成”之中。
facts.textEn: The heavenly deities command Izanagi and Izanami to make and consolidate the drifting land and grant them a heavenly jewelled spear.
facts.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
facts.sourceLocation: Sect. III, The Island of Onogoro (kj010)

facts.textZh: 伊邪那岐出现在“伊邪那岐的禊祓”之中。
facts.textEn: Deities are born as Izanagi bathes to purify himself after Yomi.
facts.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
facts.sourceLocation: Sect. X, Purification of the August Person (kj017)
